**Dominica**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-16) officially the **Commonwealth of Dominica**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-17) is an [island country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_country "Island country") in the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-English_constitution-18) It is part of the [Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands "Windward Islands") chain in the [Lesser Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles "Lesser Antilles") archipelago in the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea"). The capital, [Roseau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseau "Roseau"), is located on the western side of the island. Dominica's closest neighbours are two [constituent territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_member_state_territories_and_the_European_Union "Special member state territories and the European Union") of the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), both overseas departments of France: [Guadeloupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadeloupe "Guadeloupe") to the northwest and [Martinique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martinique "Martinique") to the south-southeast. Dominica comprises a land area of 750 km 2 (290 sq mi), and the highest point is [Morne Diablotins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morne_Diablotins "Morne Diablotins"), at 1,448 m (4,751 ft) in elevation. The population was 71,293 at the 2011 census.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-2011_census-8)

The island was settled by the [Arawak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawak "Arawak") arriving from South America in the fifth century. The [Kalinago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalinago "Kalinago") displaced the Arawak by the 15th century. [Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") is said to have passed the island on Sunday, 3rd November 1493. It was later colonised by Europeans, predominantly by the French from 1690 to 1763. The French enslaved West Africans and transported them to Dominica to work on coffee plantations. [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain") took possession in 1763 after the [Seven Years' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Years'_War "Seven Years' War") and continued the legacy of forced labor to gain wealth, and gradually established English as its official language. The island gained independence as a republic in 1978.

Dominica has been nicknamed the "Nature Island of the Caribbean" for its natural environment.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-19) It is the youngest island in the Lesser Antilles, and is still being formed by [Geothermal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geothermal_activity "Geothermal activity")-[Volcanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic "Volcanic") activity, as evidenced by the world's second-largest [hot spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_spring "Hot spring"), called [Boiling Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boiling_Lake "Boiling Lake"). The island has lush mountainous [rainforests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainforests "Rainforests") and is the home of many rare plants, animals, and bird species. There are [dry shrubland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xeric "Xeric") areas in some of the western coastal regions, but heavy rainfall occurs inland. The [Sisserou Parrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisserou_parrot "Sisserou parrot"), also known as the imperial amazon, is [critically endangered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critically_endangered "Critically endangered") and found only on Dominica. It is the island's national bird and is featured on the [National flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Dominica "Flag of Dominica"), making Dominica one of the two sovereign nations whose official flag features the color purple.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-20)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-21) The country is a member of the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations"), the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [Organization of American States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_of_American_States "Organization of American States"), the [Organisation internationale de la Francophonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_internationale_de_la_Francophonie "Organisation internationale de la Francophonie"), the [Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_of_Eastern_Caribbean_States "Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States") and the [Non-Aligned Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Aligned_Movement "Non-Aligned Movement").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The [Kalinago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalinago "Kalinago") called the island _Wai'tu kubuli_, which means "Tall is her body", likely referring to the island personified as a goddess (comparable to [Gaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaia "Gaia")).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-22)

[Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus"), sailing for [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), named the island Dominica, an abbreviation of the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language "Latin language")_[dies Dominica](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/dies%20Dominicus "wikt:dies Dominicus")_ (meaning "day of the Lord", that is, Sunday), because he first sighted the landmass on a Sunday in November 1493.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) In keeping with the Spanish pronunciation of its name,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-pronunciation_stuff-24) Dominica's name is pronounced with emphasis on the second _i_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-pronunciation_guardian-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-pronunciation_virtual-13)

The similar names and the identical [demonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demonym "Demonym") with the [Dominican Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Republic "Dominican Republic") have caused some in Dominica to advocate for a name change to Waitukubuli, which they say would contribute to further establishing the local identity[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-25) and stop mail from being wrongly sent to the Dominican Republic. Others disagree, arguing that the name change would be too expensive.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-26)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Dominica "History of Dominica")

### Geologic history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geologic history")]

Dominica first emerged from the sea during the [Oligocene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligocene "Oligocene") Epoch approximately 26 million years ago, making it the last Caribbean island to be formed by [volcanic activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanism "Volcanism") along the [Lesser Antilles Volcanic Arc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles_Volcanic_Arc "Lesser Antilles Volcanic Arc").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bg090118-27) The island remains volcanically active, with geothermal features reflecting ongoing magmatic processes beneath its surface.

### Pre-colonial period and early European contact

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Pre-colonial period and early European contact")]

Dominica's precolonial Indigenous inhabitants were the [Kalinago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalinago "Kalinago") people, who are thought to have driven out the previous [Arawak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arawak "Arawak") population.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) However, this may be a partial misconception as ancestral Kalinago narratives mention the two groups coexisting and intermarrying. The Arawak were not the primary Indigenous group. It is believed that before them were a group of paleo-Indians who arrived towards the end of the late Pleistocene period.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1493, [Christopher Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus "Christopher Columbus") first spotted the island during his [second voyage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voyages_of_Christopher_Columbus "Voyages of Christopher Columbus") to the Americas. Because he saw the island on a Sunday (November 3, 1493), Columbus named the island Dominica (Latin for 'Sunday').[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) Some Spanish colonisers settled there. But, as European explorers and settlers entered the region, Indigenous refugees from surrounding islands settled in Dominica and pushed out the Spanish settlers. The Spanish instead settled other areas that were easier to control.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### French colony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: French colony")]

Main article: [French West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_West_Indies "French West Indies")

Spain had little success in colonising Dominica. In 1632, the French [Compagnie des Îles de l'Amérique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compagnie_des_%C3%8Eles_de_l'Am%C3%A9rique "Compagnie des Îles de l'Amérique") claimed it and other _"Petites Antilles"_ for [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_France "Kingdom of France"), but no physical occupation took place.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) Between 1642 and 1650, French missionary [Raymond Breton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Breton "Raymond Breton") became the first regular European visitor to the island.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-28)

In 1660, the French and English agreed that Dominica and [St. Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_(Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines) "Saint Vincent (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)") should not be settled, but instead left to the Carib people as neutral territory.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) However, its natural resources attracted expeditions of English and French foresters, who began harvesting timber.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29) In 1690, the French established their first permanent settlements. French woodcutters from [Martinique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martinique "Martinique") and [Guadeloupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadeloupe "Guadeloupe") began to set up timber camps to supply the French islands with wood, and they gradually became permanent settlers. They brought the first enslaved Africans from West Africa to _Dominique_, as they called it in French.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1715, a revolt of impoverished white smallholders in the north of Martinique, known as La Gaoulé,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-30) caused settlers to migrate to southern Dominique, where they set up [smallholdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallholding "Smallholding"). Meanwhile, French families and others from Guadeloupe settled in the north. In 1727, the first French commander, [M. Le Grand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Le_Grand?action=edit&redlink=1 "M. Le Grand (page does not exist)"), took charge of the island with a basic French government. Dominique formally became a [colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony "Colony") of France, and the island was divided into districts or "quarters".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-31) The French had already developed plantation agriculture on Martinique and Guadeloupe, where they cultivated [sugarcane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarcane "Sugarcane") with enslaved African workers. In Dominique they gradually developed coffee plantations. Because of the trans-Atlantic slave trade, the general population came to consist primarily of black-African slaves.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1761, during the [Seven Years' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Years'_War "Seven Years' War") in Europe, a [British expedition against Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_expedition_against_Dominica "British expedition against Dominica"), led by [Andrew Rollo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Rollo,_5th_Lord_Rollo "Andrew Rollo, 5th Lord Rollo"), conquered the island and several other Caribbean islands. In 1763, France lost the war and ceded the island to Great Britain in 1763 under the [Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1763) "Treaty of Paris (1763)").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) The same year, the British established a [legislative assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislative_assembly "Legislative assembly"), with only European colonists represented. French remained the official language, but [Antillean Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antillean_Creole "Antillean Creole"), which had developed from it, was spoken by most of the population.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1778 the French, with the active co-operation of the population, began the [re-capture of Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Dominica_(1778) "Invasion of Dominica (1778)").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) This was ended in 1783 by the [second Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1783) "Treaty of Paris (1783)"), which returned the island to British control, but the island population, especially those considered _gens de couleur libres_ (lit.'free people of colour'), resisted British restrictions. The British retained control throughout French invasions in 1795 and 1805,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29) the first taking place during the period of the [Haitian Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haitian_Revolution "Haitian Revolution"), which gained the independence of Haiti (formerly Saint-Domingue, France's richest Caribbean colony).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### British colony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: British colony")]

Main articles: [British West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_West_Indies "British West Indies"), [British Leeward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Leeward_Islands "British Leeward Islands"), and [British Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Windward_Islands "British Windward Islands")

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Agostino_Brunias_-_Linen_Market%2C_Dominica_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-Agostino_Brunias_-_Linen_Market%2C_Dominica_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Agostino_Brunias_-_Linen_Market,_Dominica_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg)

A linen market in 1770s Dominica

Great Britain established a small colony in 1805. It used Dominica as part of the [Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade "Atlantic slave trade"), by which slaves were imported and sold as labour in the islands as part of a trade that included producing and shipping sugar and coffee as commodity crops to Europe. The best documented slave plantation on the island is Hillsborough Estate, which had 71 male and 68 female slaves. The [Greg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarry_Bank_Mill "Quarry Bank Mill") family were notable: Thomas Hodgson, a brother-in-law, owned a slave ship, and Thomas Greg and his brother John Greg were part-owners of [sugar plantations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_plantation "Sugar plantation") in Dominica. In January 1814, 20 slaves escaped from Hillsborough. They were recorded as recaptured and punished with 100 lashes applied to the males and 50 for the females. The slaves reportedly said that one of their people had died in the plantation hospital, and they believed he had been poisoned.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-32)

In 1831, reflecting a liberalisation of official British racial attitudes, the Brown Privilege Bill[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-33) conferred political and social rights on [free blacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_black "Free black") (mostly [free people of colour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_people_of_colour "Free people of colour"), who generally were of [mixed race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_race "Mixed race"), with African and European ancestry). With the [Slavery Abolition Act 1833](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_Abolition_Act_1833 "Slavery Abolition Act 1833"), Britain ended the institution of slavery throughout [its empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"), except in India.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-SectionLXIV-34)

With freedom came enfranchisement. In 1835, the first three men of African descent were elected to the legislative assembly of Dominica. Many slaves from the neighbouring French colonial islands of Guadeloupe and Martinique fled to Dominica. In 1838, Dominica became the first colony of the [British West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_West_Indies "British West Indies") to have an elected legislature controlled by an ethnic African majority. Most of these legislators had been free people of colour and smallholders or merchants before the abolition of slavery. Their economic and social views were different from the interests of the small, wealthy English [planter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation "Plantation") class. Reacting to a perceived threat to their power, the planters lobbied for more direct British rule.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29)

In 1865, after much agitation and tension, the colonial office replaced the elective assembly with one made up of one-half members who were elected and one-half who were appointed. Planters, who were allied with colonial administrators, outmanoeuvred the elected legislators on many occasions. In 1871, Dominica became part of the [British Leeward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Leeward_Islands "British Leeward Islands"). The political power of the elected assembly progressively eroded. [Crown colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_colony "Crown colony") government was re-established in 1896.

In [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), many Dominicans, mainly the sons of small farmers, volunteered to fight in Europe for the British Empire. After the war, an upsurge of political consciousness throughout the Caribbean led to the formation of the [Representative Government Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_historical_autonomist_and_secessionist_movements#British_West_Indies "List of historical autonomist and secessionist movements"). Marshalling public frustration with the lack of a voice in the government of Dominica, this group won one-third of the popularly elected seats of the legislative assembly in 1924, and one-half in 1936. In 1940, administration of Dominica was transferred from the [British Leeward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Leeward_Islands "British Leeward Islands") to the [British Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Windward_Islands "British Windward Islands").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29) During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), some Dominicans volunteered in British and Caribbean forces. Thousands of [Free French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_French "Free French") refugees from Martinique and Guadeloupe escaped to Dominica from the [Vichy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vichy_France "Vichy France")-controlled French islands, staying in [Roseau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseau "Roseau") and other villages.

Until 1958, Dominica was governed as part of the [British Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Windward_Islands "British Windward Islands"). Caribbean islands sought independence from 1958 to 1962, and Dominica became a province of the short-lived [West Indies Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indies_Federation "West Indies Federation") in 1958.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29) After the federation dissolved in 1962, Dominica became an associated state of the United Kingdom in 1967, and formally took responsibility for its internal affairs.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) On 3 November 1978, Dominica was granted independence as a [republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic "Republic"), led by Prime Minister [Patrick John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_John "Patrick John").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-35)

### Post-independence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Post-independence")]

In mid-1979, political discontent with founding prime minister Patrick John's administration climaxed in a civilian coup and ended in the passage of a [motion of no confidence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_of_no_confidence "Motion of no confidence") against John in the House of Assembly, Dominica's legislature, collapsing his administration. An Interim Government was formed under Dominica's second Prime Minister [Oliver Seraphin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Seraphin "Oliver Seraphin");[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) Seraphin's main task was to prepare the country for fresh general elections constitutionally due in 1980, hence the unofficial title "Interim Prime Minister". Seraphin organised and led a splinter of the Dominica Labour Party—the Democratic Labour Party—into the 1980 general election and lost mainly because his nearly 13 month-long premiership was dominated by the effects of Category Five [Hurricane David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_David "Hurricane David"), which caused 56 deaths and untold damage across the island.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-tcr3-36)[Hurricane Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Allen "Hurricane Allen") the following year caused further damage.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) After the [1980 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Dominican_general_election "1980 Dominican general election"), Seraphin's government was replaced by one led by the [Dominica Freedom Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica_Freedom_Party "Dominica Freedom Party") (DFP) under Prime Minister [Eugenia Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenia_Charles "Eugenia Charles"); she was the Caribbean's first female prime minister.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-:0-37)

In 1981, Charles's government was threatened with two attempted coups. The first was led by [Frederick Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Newton "Frederick Newton"), commander of the [Military of Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_Dominica "Military of Dominica"), who organised an attack on the police headquarters in Roseau which resulted in the death of a police officer.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-coup-38) Newton and five other soldiers were found guilty in the attack and sentenced to death in 1983; the sentences of the five accomplices were later commuted to life in prison, but Newton was executed in 1986.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-coup-38) A second occurred later in the year when the country was threatened with a takeover by [mercenaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercenaries "Mercenaries"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-39) led by [Mike Perdue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Perdue?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mike Perdue (page does not exist)") and [Wolfgang Droege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfgang_Droege "Wolfgang Droege") in [Operation Red Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Red_Dog "Operation Red Dog"). They tried to overthrow Charles as prime minister and reinstate ex-prime minister John in exchange for control over the country's development. The [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") was tipped off, and the ship hired to transport the mercenaries never left dock. The mercenaries lacked formal military experience or training, and most of the crew had been misled into joining by the ringleader Mike Perdue. [White supremacist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_supremacy "White supremacy")[Don Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Black_(white_nationalist) "Don Black (white nationalist)") was jailed for his part in the attempted coup, which violated US [neutrality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutrality_Act_of_1794 "Neutrality Act of 1794") laws.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-40)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/President_Ronald_Reagan_Meets_with_Prime_Minister_Eugenia_Charles_of_Dominica_on_Events_in_Grenada_George_Shultz_and_Robert_Mcfarlane_Also_Visible_-_DPLA_-_b2115fa33fa49a111b0a71dd2acfb384.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Ronald_Reagan_Meets_with_Prime_Minister_Eugenia_Charles_of_Dominica_on_Events_in_Grenada_George_Shultz_and_Robert_Mcfarlane_Also_Visible_-_DPLA_-_b2115fa33fa49a111b0a71dd2acfb384.jpg)

[Eugenia Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenia_Charles "Eugenia Charles"), Prime Minister 1980–95, discussing the [situation in Grenada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Grenada "United States invasion of Grenada") in 1983 with US President [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan")

The Charles government supported the 1983 American [invasion of Grenada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Grenada "Invasion of Grenada"), earning Dominica praise from the US government of [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan"), and an increase in financial aid.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-41)

By the middle of the 1980s, the economy had begun to recover,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) before weakening again due to a decrease in [banana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banana "Banana") prices. Eugenia Charles won the [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Dominican_general_election "1985 Dominican general election") general election, becoming the first incumbent Dominica Prime Minister to be popularly re-elected. The continuing downturn in the economy and the tight grip by Eugenia Charles on Dominica politics gave rise to a self-titled "Third Force" political formation in 1988, which disrupted the traditional two-party arrangement of governing DFP and opposition DLP. The formation soon formalised as the [United Workers' Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UWP_(Dominica)?action=edit&redlink=1 "UWP (Dominica) (page does not exist)") (UWP) and selected as its leader [Edison James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edison_James "Edison James"), the former general manager of the Dominica Banana Marketing Company. This was a strategic selection: he had prestige among banana farmers, and support from his origins in the East Coast, which had begun to feel alienated by the West Coast elites in Roseau, Dominica's capital.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29) Eugenia Charles again won the [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_Dominican_general_election "1990 Dominican general election") general election, the first incumbent Dominica prime minister to win three consecutive general elections, but the UWP's emergence had reduced her party's majority in Parliament to one. It was, therefore, no great surprise when Eugenia Charles gave up political leadership of the Dominica Freedom Party in 1993 and did not contest the 1995 general election in any capacity. No longer benefitting from her leadership, the Dominica Freedom Party lost the [1995 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Dominican_general_election "1995 Dominican general election") to the UWP, and James became prime minister.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) He attempted to diversify the Dominican economy away from over-reliance on bananas. The crop was largely destroyed by [Hurricane Luis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Luis "Hurricane Luis") in 1995,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) and James was unable to restore the banana industry to its former selling price and prestige. Moreover, his administration became embroiled in opposition charges of official corruption.

In the [31 January 2000 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Dominican_general_election "2000 Dominican general election"), the UWP were defeated by a coalition of the DLP, led by left-leaning [Roosevelt B. "Rosie" Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_Douglas "Rosie Douglas"), and the DFP led by former trade union leader [Charles Savarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Savarin "Charles Savarin"); Douglas became prime minister. One UWP member of the House of Assembly [crossed the floor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossing_the_floor "Crossing the floor"), joining the DLP–DFP coalition government. Douglas died on 1 October 2000 after only a few months in office,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-42) and was replaced by [Pierre Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Charles_(Dominican_politician) "Pierre Charles (Dominican politician)"), who died in office on 6 January 2004.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-43)[Roosevelt Skerrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_Skerrit "Roosevelt Skerrit"), also of the DLP, replaced Pierre Charles as prime minister, becoming the world's youngest head of government at the age of 31.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) Under Skerrit's leadership, the DLP won [elections in May 2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Dominican_general_election "2005 Dominican general election") that gave the party 12 seats in the 21-seat Parliament. The UWP won 8 seats and Ronald Toulon, who was an independent candidate at that time, won the remaining seat. Later, Toulon joined the government.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-44) With his 2005 election win, Skerrit became only the second incumbent prime minister to be popularly re-elected.

In the [2009 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Dominican_general_election "2009 Dominican general election"), the DLP won 18 of 21 seats. The UWP claimed campaign improprieties and embarked on a wide range of protest actions, including boycott of Parliament. UWP's boycott caused at least three unauthorised absences from Parliament for two of their three elected representatives in violation of Parliamentary procedure, leading to their two seats being declared vacant and by-elections called to fill them in July 2010 The UWP held both seats.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-45) The DLP under Skerrit went on to win the [2014 Dominican general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Dominican_general_election "2014 Dominican general election").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CE-46)

On 17 September 2012 [Eliud Thaddeus Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Williams "Eliud Williams") was sworn in as president (a largely ceremonial role), replacing [Dr. Nicholas Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Liverpool "Nicholas Liverpool") who was reportedly removed from office due to ill health. On 30 September 2013 former trade union leader and former DFP leader [Charles Savarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Savarin "Charles Savarin") was elected president, having only days before resigned as a minister of government. He is Dominica's eighth president.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-47)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/Morning_after_Hurricane_Maria_%2837372721465%29.jpg/250px-Morning_after_Hurricane_Maria_%2837372721465%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Morning_after_Hurricane_Maria_(37372721465).jpg)

Damage in [Roseau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseau "Roseau") caused by Hurricane Maria in 2017

[Tropical Storm Erika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Erika "Tropical Storm Erika") devastated the island in August 2015, killing 30 and causing severe environmental and economic damage.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) Dominica was again struck on 18 September 2017, suffering a direct landfall from Category 5 [Hurricane Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Maria "Hurricane Maria").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-48) Early estimates of damage suggested 90% of the buildings on the island had been destroyed, with infrastructure left in ruins.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-49)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Handy-50) The UK, France and the Netherlands set up shipping and air lifts to take aid to the island, the scale of destruction having left most people homeless.

President Charles Angelo Savarin was re-elected in 2018 for a new five-year term.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-51) In December 2019, incumbent prime minister Roosevelt Skerrit won his fourth consecutive general [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Dominican_general_election "2019 Dominican general election") 18 seats to 3, becoming the first prime minister of Dominica to do so.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-52)

Dominica won its first two Commonwealth Games medals in silver (men's triple jump) and bronze (women's triple jump) in the [2018 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Commonwealth_Games "2018 Commonwealth Games") on the [Gold Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast,_Queensland "Gold Coast, Queensland").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-53) Dominica received its first Olympic gold medal in the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") when [Thea LaFond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thea_LaFond "Thea LaFond") won the [women's triple jump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_triple_jump "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's triple jump") with a length of 15.02 metres.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Geography")]

Main article: [Geography of Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Dominica "Geography of Dominica")

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Map_of_Dominica.gif/250px-Map_of_Dominica.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Map_of_Dominica.gif)

Map of Dominica.

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Lesser_Antilles_250m.jpg/250px-Lesser_Antilles_250m.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lesser_Antilles_250m.jpg)

Satellite photograph of Dominica in the center, with [Guadeloupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadeloupe "Guadeloupe") to the north and [Martinique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martinique "Martinique") to the south

Dominica is an [island nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_nation "Island nation") in the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea"), the northernmost of the [Windward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands "Windward Islands") (though it is sometimes considered the southernmost of the [Leeward Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward_Islands "Leeward Islands")).[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-britannica.com-54) The size of the country is about 750 km 2 (289.5 sq mi) and it is about 47 km (29 mi) long and 26 km (16 mi) wide.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4)

Known as "The Nature Island of the Caribbean"[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-55)[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] due to its lush scenery and varied flora and fauna, Dominica is largely covered by [rainforest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainforest "Rainforest") and is home to the world's second-largest [hot spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_spring "Hot spring"), [Boiling Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boiling_Lake "Boiling Lake").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-56)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-57) Within its borders lie two ecoregions: Windward Islands' moist forests and Windward Islands' [xeric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deserts_and_xeric_shrublands "Deserts and xeric shrublands") scrub.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-58) The most mountainous of the Lesser Antilles, its volcanic peaks are cones of lava craters, the largest of these being (north-to-south) [Morne aux Diables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morne_aux_Diables "Morne aux Diables"), [Morne Diablotins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morne_Diablotins "Morne Diablotins") (the highest on the island at 1,447 m (4,747 ft)),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4)[Morne Trois Pitons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morne_Trois_Pitons "Morne Trois Pitons") and [Morne Anglais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morne_Anglais?action=edit&redlink=1 "Morne Anglais (page does not exist)"). [Morne Trois Pitons National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morne_Trois_Pitons_National_Park "Morne Trois Pitons National Park") is a tropical forest blended with volcanic features;[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-59) it was recognised as a [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") on 4 April 1995, a distinction it shares with four other Caribbean islands.[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-60) The [Calibishie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calibishie "Calibishie") area in the country's northeast has sandy beaches.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-61) Some plants and animals thought to be extinct on surrounding islands can still be found in Dominica's forests.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-62) The island has several [protected areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protected_area "Protected area"), including [Cabrits National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabrits_National_Park "Cabrits National Park"), as well as 365 rivers. For a few years the government sought to encourage the island as an [ecotourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecotourism "Ecotourism") destination, although the hurricane of 2017 has since changed these plans.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4) The country had a 2018 [Forest Landscape Integrity Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index "Forest Landscape Integrity Index") mean score of 1.06/10, ranking it 166th globally out of 172 countries.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-63)

There are two primary population centres: the capital [Roseau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseau "Roseau") (with 14,725 inhabitants in 2011) and [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth,_Dominica "Portsmouth, Dominica") (with 4,167 inhabitants in 2011). The main centres tend to be located around the coast, with the mountainous interior sparsely populated.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4)

Dominica is especially vulnerable to [hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane "Hurricane") as the island is located in what is referred to as the hurricane region.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4) In 1979, [Hurricane David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_David "Hurricane David") struck the island as a Category 4 hurricane, causing widespread and extreme damage. On 17 August 2007, [Hurricane Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dean "Hurricane Dean"), a Category 1 hurricane at the time, hit the island. A mother and her seven-year-old son died when a [landslide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landslide "Landslide") caused by the heavy rains crushed their house.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Forbes_Haiti_preps-64) In another incident two people were injured when a tree fell on their house.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-cbc_2007-08-17-65)[Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Dominica "Prime Minister of Dominica")[Roosevelt Skerrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_Skerrit "Roosevelt Skerrit") estimated that 100 to 125 homes were damaged, and that the agricultural sector was extensively damaged, in particular the banana crop.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-cbc_2007-08-17_02-66) In August 2015, [Tropical Storm Erika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Erika "Tropical Storm Erika") caused extensive flooding and landslides across the island. Multiple communities were evacuated and upwards of 30 people were killed.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-67) According to a Rapid Damage and Impact Assessment prepared for Dominica by the World Bank, the total damage and losses from the storm were US$484.82 million or 90% of Dominica's yearly GDP.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-68) Category 5 [Hurricane Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Maria "Hurricane Maria") struck the island in 2017 and caused losses of approximately US$930 million or 226% of GDP.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Handy-50)

### Fauna

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Fauna")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Amazona_imperialis_Mitchell.jpg/250px-Amazona_imperialis_Mitchell.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Amazona_imperialis_Mitchell.jpg)

Imperial Amazon

Dominica is home to 200 bird species, including two species [endemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemism "Endemism") to the island _.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite\_note-69)_ The [sisserou parrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_amazon "Imperial amazon") (_Amazona imperialis_) is Dominica's national bird and is endemic to its mountain forests.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) A related species, the jaco or [red-necked parrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red-necked_parrot "Red-necked parrot") (_A. arausiaca_), is also endemic to the island.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23) Both birds are rare and protected, though some forests are still threatened by logging in addition to the long-standing threat of hurricanes.

Dominica has recorded four species of snakes,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-:1-70) including two endemic species: the [Dominican blind snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_blind_snake "Dominican blind snake")[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-71) and the [Dominican boa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boa_nebulosa "Boa nebulosa").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-72) The island is home to eleven species of lizards,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-:1-70) including two endemic species: the [Dominican anole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anolis_oculatus "Anolis oculatus") and the [Dominican ground lizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_ground_lizard "Dominican ground lizard").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-73)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-74)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-75) Dominica is the last major stronghold of the [critically endangered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critically_endangered "Critically endangered")[Lesser Antillean iguana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antillean_iguana "Lesser Antillean iguana") (_Iguana delicatissima_).[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-van_den_BurgBrisbaneKnapp2019-76)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-77)

The [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea") around the island of Dominica is home to many [cetaceans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetacean "Cetacean").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-78) A group of [sperm whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm_whale "Sperm whale") live in the area year-round.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-79) Other cetaceans commonly seen in the area include [spinner dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinner_dolphin "Spinner dolphin"), [pantropical spotted dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pantropical_spotted_dolphin "Pantropical spotted dolphin") and [bottlenose dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bottlenose_dolphin "Bottlenose dolphin").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-80)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-81)

Less commonly seen animals include [killer whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killer_whales "Killer whales"), [false killer whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_killer_whale "False killer whale"), [pygmy sperm whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pygmy_sperm_whale "Pygmy sperm whale"), [dwarf sperm whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwarf_sperm_whale "Dwarf sperm whale"), [Risso's dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risso's_dolphin "Risso's dolphin"), [common dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_dolphin "Common dolphin"), [Atlantic spotted dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_spotted_dolphin "Atlantic spotted dolphin"), [humpback whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humpback_whales "Humpback whales") and [Bryde's whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryde's_whale "Bryde's whale").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] This makes Dominica a destination for tourists interested in [whale-watching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whale-watching "Whale-watching").

Dominica is a [parliamentary democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_democracy "Parliamentary democracy") within the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-English_constitution-18) The capital is [Roseau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseau "Roseau"). Dominica is one of the Caribbean's few [republics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic "Republic"). The [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") is an indirectly elected [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Dominica "President of Dominica"), while executive power rests with the [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Dominica "Cabinet of Dominica"), headed by the [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Dominica "Prime Minister of Dominica").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-English_constitution-18) The [unicameral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicameral "Unicameral")[parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament "Parliament") consists of the 30-member [House of Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Assembly_of_Dominica "House of Assembly of Dominica"), which consists of 21 directly elected members, and 9 senators who may either be appointed by the president or elected by the other members of the House of Assembly.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-English_constitution-18)

Unlike other former British colonies in the region, Dominica has never been a [Commonwealth realm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_realm "Commonwealth realm"), having become a republic upon gaining its independence. Dominica is a full and participating member of the [Caribbean Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Community "Caribbean Community") (CARICOM) and the [Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_of_Eastern_Caribbean_States "Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States") (OECS).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)

Dominica is also a member of the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court"), with a [Bilateral Immunity Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilateral_Immunity_Agreement "Bilateral Immunity Agreement") of protection with the US military, as covered under [Article 98](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_Statute_of_the_International_Criminal_Court "Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court"). In January 2008, Dominica joined the [Bolivarian Alternative for the Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivarian_Alternative_for_the_Americas "Bolivarian Alternative for the Americas").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica_-_Dominica-23)

In 2025, the government of Dominica signed a free movement cooperation agreement along with Barbados, [Belize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belize "Belize"), and [Saint Vincent and the Grenadines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines "Saint Vincent and the Grenadines") allowing each other's nationals to have free movement between their nations just by presenting their passport and indicating the intention to become a full national with intention to work at time of entry.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-82)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-83)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-84)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-85)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-86)

### Territorial disputes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Territorial disputes")]

Dominica is engaged in a long-running dispute with [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela") over Venezuela's territorial claims to the sea surrounding [Isla de Aves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isla_de_Aves "Isla de Aves") (literally Bird Island, but in fact called 'Bird Rock' by Dominican authorities),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-MitchellGold1983-87) a tiny islet located 140 mi (225 km) west of the island of Dominica.

During a visit to Venezuela, Dominica's Prime Minister [Roosevelt Skerrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_Skerrit "Roosevelt Skerrit"), in June 2006, stated, "Aves Island belongs to Venezuela.", unofficially ending the territorial claim.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-88)

### Military

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Military")]

There has been no [standing army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_army "Standing army") in Dominica since 1981 when the [Dominican Defence Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Defence_Force?action=edit&redlink=1 "Dominican Defence Force (page does not exist)") was disbanded following two violent coup attempts against [Eugenia Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenia_Charles "Eugenia Charles").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-89)

The civil [Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Dominica_Police_Force "Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force") includes a Special Service Unit[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-90) and [Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast_guard "Coast guard"). In the event of war or other emergency, if proclaimed by the authorities, the Police Force shall be a military force which may be employed for State defence (_Police Act_, Chapter 14:01).[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-91)

Dominica is a member of the [Regional Security System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Security_System "Regional Security System") (RSS).

### LGBT rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: LGBT rights")]

Both male and female [same-sex sexual activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Dominica "LGBT rights in Dominica") were criminalised in Dominica in the 19th century during the colonial era.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-92)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-93) In April 2024, Dominican attorney-at-law [Cara Shillingford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cara_Shillingford "Cara Shillingford") persuaded the High Court of Justice to overturn the laws banning same-sex activity[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-94) since they violated LGBT individuals' constitutional rights.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-95)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Economy")]

Main article: [Economy of Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Dominica "Economy of Dominica")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Dominica_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg/250px-Dominica_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dominica_Product_Exports_(2019).svg)

Dominica product exports (2019)

Dominica's currency is the [East Caribbean Dollar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Caribbean_Dollar "East Caribbean Dollar"). In 2008, Dominica had one of the lowest [per capita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita "Per capita")[gross domestic product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") (GDP) rates of Eastern Caribbean states.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-96)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-97) The country nearly had a financial crisis in 2003 and 2004, but Dominica's economy grew by 3.5% in 2005 and 4.0% in 2006, following a decade of poor performance. Growth in 2006 was attributed to gains in tourism, construction, offshore and other services, and some sub-sectors of the banana industry. Around this time the [International Monetary Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") (IMF) praised the Government of Dominica for its successful macroeconomic reforms, but also pointed out remaining challenges, including the need for further reductions in public debt, increased financial sector regulation, and market diversification.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29)

Agriculture, especially bananas, once dominated Dominica's economy,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4) and nearly one-third of the labour force worked in agriculture in the early 2000s. The sector, however, is highly vulnerable to weather conditions and to external events affecting commodity prices. In 2007, [Hurricane Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dean "Hurricane Dean") caused significant damage to the agricultural sector as well as the country's infrastructure, especially roads.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In response to reduced [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") (EU) [trade preferences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_preference "Trade preference") for bananas from the former European colonies after the 2009 [WTO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTO "WTO") decision,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-98)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-99)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-100)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-101) the government has diversified the agricultural sector by promoting the production of coffee, [patchouli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patchouli "Patchouli"), [aloe vera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloe_vera "Aloe vera"), cut flowers, and exotic fruits such as mango, guava and papaya,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] while the economy has become increasingly dependent on tourism.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-CIA_World_Factbook_-_Dominica-4)

The expected increase of Dominica's [Citizenship by Investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigrant_investor_programs "Immigrant investor programs") (CBI) fees has been suspended with no implementation date in sight, as announced by Prime Minister Roosevelt Skerrit, in the 2016 budget speech.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-102)

### International trade

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: International trade")]

Dominica is a beneficiary of the [Caribbean Basin Initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Basin_Initiative "Caribbean Basin Initiative") (CBI) that grants duty-free entry into the United States for many goods. Dominica also belongs to the predominantly English-speaking [Caribbean Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Community "Caribbean Community") (CARICOM), the [CARICOM Single Market and Economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARICOM_Single_Market_and_Economy "CARICOM Single Market and Economy") (CSME), and the [Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_of_Eastern_Caribbean_States "Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States") (OECS).[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-bn-29)

### Financial services industry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Financial services industry")]

[![Image 20: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **needs [more citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")**. Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability")._(January 2025)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

Dominica is becoming in recent years[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] a major international financial centre, including [offshore banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_banking "Offshore banking"), [payment processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_processing "Payment processing") companies, and general corporate activities.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-103) Regulation and supervision of the [financial services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_services "Financial services") industry is the responsibility of the [Financial Service Unit of the Commonwealth of Dominica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Service_Unit_of_the_Commonwealth_of_Dominica "Financial Service Unit of the Commonwealth of Dominica") (FSU) under the supervision of the Ministry of Finance. There are a number of service providers. These include global financial institutions including [Scotiabank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotiabank "Scotiabank"), [Royal Bank of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Bank_of_Canada "Royal Bank of Canada"), [Cathedral Investment Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_Investment_Bank "Cathedral Investment Bank"), [First Caribbean International Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Caribbean_International_Bank "First Caribbean International Bank"), and The Interoceanic Bank of the Caribbean.

Starting in the mid-late 1990s, [offshore financial centres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_financial_centres "Offshore financial centres"), such as Dominica, came under increasing pressure from the [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD "OECD") for their allegedly harmful tax regimes, where the OECD wished to prevent low-tax regimes from having an advantage in the global marketplace. The OECD threatened to place Dominica and other [financial centres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_centres "Financial centres") on a "black list" and impose sanctions against them. Dominica successfully avoided being placed on the OECD black list by committing to regulatory reform to improve transparency and begin information exchange with OECD member countries about their citizens.

Dominica supposedly offers tax-free status to companies relocating from abroad. It is not known how many companies benefit from the tax-free status because of the strict confidentiality the government enforces, although it is known many Internet businesses and [hedge funds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_fund "Hedge fund") utilise Dominica for this reason. On 12 July 2012 Dominica signed an agreement with Poland to exchange tax information.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-104)

### Economic immigrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Economic immigrants")]

Main article: [Dominica citizenship by investment programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica_citizenship_by_investment_programme "Dominica citizenship by investment programme")

Dominica offers an official and legally mandated [economic citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_citizenship "Economic citizenship") to those seeking a valid second citizenship. The nationality law of Dominica authorises the government to waive the normal requirement of seven years of legal residence to acquire citizenship in exchange for an investment into their country's economy. The required contribution for a main applicant starts at US$100,000 through the Economic Diversification Fund.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-105) Alternatively, since 2014, applicants can make a US$200,000 minimum investment in pre-approved real estate from island exclusive resorts or global brands like Marriott, Kempinski or Hilton.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-106) According to officials, the [citizenship by investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship_by_investment "Citizenship by investment") (CBI) programme was an economic and fiscal "lifeline" in the aftermaths of Tropical Storm Erika in 2015 and Hurricane Maria in 2017, and its new investment option had become the main source of [Foreign Direct Investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Direct_Investment "Foreign Direct Investment") into Dominica by early 2016.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-107) Dominican citizens can travel without a visa, or obtain a visa upon entry, to nearly 140 countries and territories, including the UK and the Schengen Zone.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-108) Applying for Dominican citizenship requires interacting with official Government Approved Economic Citizenship Agents as the first step in the application process.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-109) This programme is valued at 16% of the government's total revenue as of 2018[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dominica&action=edit).[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-110)

The government's management of the economic citizenship programme and an initial perceived lack of transparency in the use of the revenues generated are a frequent topic of heated domestic political controversy. Referring to the opposition, prime minister Skerrit in 2016 stated, "If they can discredit the Citizenship by Investment Program and make Dominica an unattractive place to obtain citizenship, then revenues would fall and the government would not be able to rebuild the country. Or, the government would then have to increase taxes on the people; making itself unpopular in their sight."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-111) Since then, the Government of Dominica has improved transparency of CBI funds. According to prime minister Skerrit's 2018–2019 Budget Address,[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-112) the island's CBI Programme has helped develop a national health insurance pilot that provides Dominican children in critical medical conditions with overseas treatment. Because many residents were displaced by Hurricane Maria's impact on the small Caribbean island, the government pledged to build 5,000 hurricane-proof homes, of which the first batch of 125 houses were scheduled for occupancy in February 2019.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-113) The CBI Programme has also significantly helped to develop and create jobs in the island's ecotourism sector.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-114) Furthermore, the Skerrit administration set aside EC$5m every month for the construction of a new airport.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-115)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-116)

The _[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial\_Times "Financial Times")_'s _Professional Wealth Management_ publication ranked Dominica as the world's best citizenship-by-investment programme in its annual CBI Index.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-117)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-118) According to the report, investors choose Dominica's citizenship because it has the most affordable investment threshold and, while the security checks each applicant is subjected to remain very strict,[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-119) the application process is straightforward and streamlined.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica#cite_note-120)
