### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

Seychelles was uninhabited throughout most of recorded history, although simulations of [Austronesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austronesian_peoples "Austronesian peoples") migration patterns indicate a good probability that they visited the islands.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-23) Tombs visible until 1910 at Anse Lascars on Silhouette Island have also been conjectured to belong to later [Maldivian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldivians "Maldivians") and [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs "Arabs") traders visiting the archipelago.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-24)[Vasco da Gama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama "Vasco da Gama") and his [4th Portuguese India Armada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_Portuguese_India_Armada_(Gama,_1502) "4th Portuguese India Armada (Gama, 1502)") discovered the Seychelles on 15 March 1503; the first sighting was made by [Thomé Lopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thom%C3%A9_Lopes "Thomé Lopes") aboard _Rui Mendes de Brito_. Da Gama's ships passed close to an elevated island, probably [Silhouette Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silhouette_Island "Silhouette Island"), and the following day [Desroches Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desroches_Island "Desroches Island"). Later, the Portuguese mapped a group of seven islands and named them _The Seven Sisters._[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-25) The earliest recorded landing was in January 1609, by the crew of the _Ascension_ under Captain [Alexander Sharpeigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Sharpeigh "Alexander Sharpeigh") during the fourth voyage of the British [East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company "East India Company").

A transit point for trade between Africa and Asia, the islands were said to be occasionally used by pirates until the French began to take control in 1756 when a Stone of Possession was laid on [Mahé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mah%C3%A9 "Mahé") by Captain [Corneille Nicholas Morphey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneille_Nicholas_Morphey "Corneille Nicholas Morphey"). The islands were named after French politician [Jean Moreau de Séchelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Moreau_de_S%C3%A9chelles "Jean Moreau de Séchelles"), and were formally part of the colony of [Isle de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_de_France_(Mauritius) "Isle de France (Mauritius)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-26) In August 1770, the French ship _Thélémaque_ under Captain Leblanc Lécore landed 15 white settlers and 13 African and Indian slaves on [Ste. Anne Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ste._Anne_Island "Ste. Anne Island").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-27)

During the [French Revolutionary Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Wars "French Revolutionary Wars"), the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") frigate [HMS _Orpheus_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Orpheus_(1780) "HMS Orpheus (1780)") under Captain Henry Newcombe arrived at Mahé on 16 May 1794. [Jean-Baptiste Quéau de Quinssy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Baptiste_Qu%C3%A9au_de_Quinssy?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jean-Baptiste Quéau de Quinssy (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Baptiste%20Qu%C3%A9au%20de%20Quinssy "fr:Jean-Baptiste Quéau de Quinssy")], the senior administrator in the Seychelles, refused to resist _Orpheus_ and instead successfully negotiated with the British, resulting the islands remaining under French control as "neutral" territory. After British forces completed their [invasion of Isle de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Isle_de_France "Invasion of Isle de France") in December 1810, they assumed control over the Seychelles, which was formalised in the 1814 [Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1814) "Treaty of Paris (1814)") that ended the [War of the Sixth Coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Sixth_Coalition "War of the Sixth Coalition"). Seychelles became a separate [crown colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_colony "Crown colony") from Mauritius in 1903. [Elections in Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elections_in_Seychelles "Elections in Seychelles") were held in 1966 and 1970.

### Independence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Independence")]

In 1976, Seychelles gained independence from the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") as a republic. It has since become a member of the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-History_of_Seychelles-28) In the 1970s Seychelles was "the place to be seen, a playground for film stars and the international jet set".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29) In 1977, a [coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Seychelles_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1977 Seychelles coup d'état") by [France-Albert René](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France-Albert_Ren%C3%A9 "France-Albert René") ousted the first president of the republic, [James Mancham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Mancham "James Mancham").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-africanhistory.about.com-30) René discouraged over-dependence on tourism and declared that he wanted "to keep Seychelles for the Seychellois".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29)

The 1979 constitution declared a [socialist one-party state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_party_rule_in_Seychelles "One party rule in Seychelles"), which lasted until 1991.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-31)

In the 1980s there were a series of coup attempts against President René, some of which were supported by South Africa. In 1981, [Mike Hoare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Hoare "Mike Hoare") led a team of 43 South African mercenaries masquerading as holidaying rugby players in the [1981 Seychelles coup d'état attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Seychelles_coup_d'%C3%A9tat_attempt "1981 Seychelles coup d'état attempt").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29) There was a gun battle at the airport, and most of the mercenaries later escaped in a hijacked [Air India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_India "Air India") plane.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29) The leader of this hijacking was German mercenary D. Clodo, a former member of the [Rhodesian SAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Special_Air_Service "Rhodesian Special Air Service").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-32) Clodo later stood trial in South Africa (where he was acquitted) as well as in his home country Germany for air piracy.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-33)

In 1986, an attempted coup led by the Seychelles Minister of Defence, Ogilvy Berlouis, caused President René to request assistance from India. In [Operation Flowers are Blooming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Flowers_are_Blooming "Operation Flowers are Blooming"), the Indian Navy's [_Nilgiri_-class frigate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilgiri-class_frigate_(1972) "Nilgiri-class frigate (1972)")[_Vindhyagiri_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vindhyagiri_(F42) "INS Vindhyagiri (F42)") arrived in Port Victoria to help avert the coup.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-34)

The first draft of a new constitution failed to receive the requisite 60% of voters in 1992, but an amended version was approved in 1993.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-35)

In January 2013, Seychelles declared a state of emergency when the tropical [cyclone Felleng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Felleng "Cyclone Felleng") caused torrential rain, and flooding and landslides destroyed hundreds of houses.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-UN-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-AL-37)

Following the coup in 1977, the president always represented the same political party until the October [2020 Seychellois general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Seychellois_general_election "2020 Seychellois general election"), which was historic in that the opposition party won. [Wavel Ramkalawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavel_Ramkalawan "Wavel Ramkalawan") was the first president who did not represent United Seychelles (the current name of the former Seychelles People's Progressive Front).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-38)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-39)

In January 2023, Seychelles announced its final stages of completing its marine spatial plan. It would become the second largest ocean area at 1.35 million km 2 (520,000 sq mi) behind [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway"), in support of its [blue economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_economy "Blue economy").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-40)

In October 2025, [presidential runoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Seychellois_general_election "2025 Seychellois general election") was won by former parliamentary speaker and main opposition leader, [Patrick Herminie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Herminie "Patrick Herminie"), meaning Herminie's party, [United Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Seychelles "United Seychelles") (US) returned to power.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-41) On 26 October 2025, Patrick Herminie was sworn in as Seychelles' sixth president.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-reuters.com-42)

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Politics")]

Main article: [Politics of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Seychelles "Politics of Seychelles")

The Seychelles president, who is [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government"), is elected by popular vote for a five-year term of office. The cabinet is presided over and appointed by the president, subject to the approval of a majority of the legislature. As of 2026, the president is [Patrick Herminie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Herminie "Patrick Herminie").

The [unicameral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicameral "Unicameral") Seychellois parliament, the [National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_(Seychelles) "National Assembly (Seychelles)") or _Assemblée Nationale_, consists of 35 members, 26 of whom are elected directly by popular vote, while the remaining nine seats are appointed proportionally according to the percentage of votes received by each party. All members serve five-year terms.

The [Supreme Court of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Seychelles "Supreme Court of Seychelles"), created in 1903, is the highest trial court in Seychelles and the first court of appeal from all the lower courts and tribunals. The highest court of law in Seychelles is the Seychelles Court of Appeal, which is the court of final appeal in the country.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-43)

### Political culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Political culture")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/James_Michel_in_meeting.jpg/250px-James_Michel_in_meeting.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Michel_in_meeting.jpg)

President [James Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Michel "James Michel") in his office in [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles"), 2009

Seychelles' long-term president [France-Albert René](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France-Albert_Ren%C3%A9 "France-Albert René") came to power after his supporters overthrew the first president [James Mancham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Mancham "James Mancham") on 5 June 1977 in a [coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_d'%C3%A9tat "Coup d'état") and installed him as president. René was at that time the prime minister. René ruled as a [strongman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strongman_(politics) "Strongman (politics)") under a [socialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist "Socialist")[one-party system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-party_system "One-party system") until 1993, when he was forced to introduce a multi-party system. He stepped down in 2004 in favour of his vice-president, [James Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Michel "James Michel"), who was re-elected in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Seychellois_presidential_election "2006 Seychellois presidential election"), [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Seychellois_presidential_election "2011 Seychellois presidential election") and again in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Seychellois_presidential_election "2015 Seychellois presidential election").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-44)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Seychelles_Nation-45)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Reuters-46)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Agence_France-Presse-47) On 28 September 2016, the Office of the President announced that Michel would step down effective 16 October, and that Vice President [Danny Faure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Faure "Danny Faure") would complete the rest of Michel's term.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-48)

On 26 October 2020, [Wavel Ramkalawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavel_Ramkalawan "Wavel Ramkalawan"), a 59-year-old Anglican priest, was elected the fifth President of the Republic of Seychelles. Ramkalawan was an opposition MP from 1993 to 2011, and from 2016 to 2020. He served as the [Leader of the Opposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Opposition_(Seychelles) "Leader of the Opposition (Seychelles)") from 1998 to 2011 and from 2016 to 2020. Ramkalawan defeated incumbent Danny Faure by 54.9% to 43.5%. This marked the first time the opposition had won a presidential election in Seychelles.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-49)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-50)

The primary political parties are the former long-time ruling socialist [People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Party_(Seychelles) "People's Party (Seychelles)") (PP), known until 2009 as the Seychelles People's Progressive Front (SPPF) now called [United Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Seychelles "United Seychelles") (US), and the [socially liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_liberalism "Social liberalism")[Seychelles National Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_National_Party "Seychelles National Party") (SNP).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-51)

The [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Seychellois_general_election "2020 Seychellois general election") of the National Assembly was held on 22–24 October 2020. The Seychelles National Party, the Seychelles Party for Social Justice and Democracy and the Seychelles United Party formed a coalition, [Linyon Demokratik Seselwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linyon_Demokratik_Seselwa "Linyon Demokratik Seselwa") (LDS). LDS won 25 seats and US got 10 seats of the 35 seats of the National Assembly.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-52) However, in the 2025 Seychellois general [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Seychellois_general_election "2025 Seychellois general election") United Seychelles won 15 out of 26 seats in the parliament.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-53)

### Foreign relations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Foreign relations")]

Further information: [Foreign relations of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Seychelles "Foreign relations of Seychelles")

Seychelles is a member of the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union"), the [Indian Ocean Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_Commission "Indian Ocean Commission"), [La Francophonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Francophonie "La Francophonie"), the [Southern African Development Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_African_Development_Community "Southern African Development Community") and the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").

Between 1979 and 1983, various plots to overthrow the non-aligned government of France-Albert René were, according to leading participants, supported by the United States, France, and South Africa. Commonly cited reasons for such attempts include René's socialist politics, his non-aligned stance toward the Western and Eastern Blocs, and the United States' military lease in the country, which was set to expire in 1990. All coup efforts in this period failed.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-54) Under the Obama administration, the US began running drone operations out of Seychelles.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-:0-55) In the Spring of 2013, members of the [Special-Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Purpose_Marine_Air-Ground_Task_Force_%E2%80%93_Crisis_Response_%E2%80%93_Africa "Special Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force – Crisis Response – Africa") mentored troops in Seychelles, along with a variety of other African nations.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-:0-55)

### Military

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Military")]

Main article: [Seychelles People's Defence Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_People's_Defence_Force "Seychelles People's Defence Force")

The [military of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_Seychelles "Military of Seychelles") is the [Seychelles People's Defence Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_People's_Defence_Force "Seychelles People's Defence Force") which consists of a number of distinct branches: an infantry unit and coast guard, air force and a presidential protection unit. India has played and continues to play a key role in developing the military of Seychelles. After handing over two [SDB Mk5 patrol vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinkat-class_patrol_vessel "Trinkat-class patrol vessel") built by [GRSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GRSE "GRSE"), the INS _Tarasa_ and INS _Tarmugli_, to the [Seychelles Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_Coast_Guard "Seychelles Coast Guard"), which were subsequently renamed [PS _Constant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PS_Constant "PS Constant") and [PS _Topaz_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PS_Topaz "PS Topaz"), India also gifted a [Dornier 228](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dornier_228 "Dornier 228") aircraft built by [Hindustan Aeronautics Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan_Aeronautics_Limited "Hindustan Aeronautics Limited").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-56) India also signed a pact to develop [Assumption Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Island "Assumption Island"). Spread over 11 km 2 (4 sq mi), it is strategically located in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean"), north of [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar "Madagascar"). The island is being leased for the development of strategic assets by India.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-57) In 2018, Seychelles signed the UN [Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_on_the_Prohibition_of_Nuclear_Weapons "Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-58)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-59)

### Incarceration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Incarceration")]

Further information: [List of countries by incarceration rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_incarceration_rate "List of countries by incarceration rate")

In 2014, Seychelles had the highest incarceration rate in the world of 799 prisoners per 100,000 population, exceeding the United States' rate by 15%.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-60) However, the country's actual population was less than 100,000; as of September 2014, Seychelles had 735 actual prisoners, 6% of whom were female and were incarcerated in three prisons.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-61)

The incarceration rate in Seychelles has since dropped significantly. It is no longer among the top ten countries with the highest rate of incarceration. In 2022, the incarceration rate was 287 per 100,000 population, being just the 31st highest in the world.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-62)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

### Modern piracy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Modern piracy")]

Seychelles is a key participant in the fight against Indian Ocean [piracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracy "Piracy") primarily committed by [Somali pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracy_off_the_coast_of_Somalia#Effects_and_perceptions "Piracy off the coast of Somalia").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-wc-63) Former president [James Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Michel "James Michel") said that piracy costs between $7 million – $12 million a year to the international community: "The pirates cost 4% of the Seychelles [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product"), including direct and indirect costs for the loss of boats, fishing, and tourism, and the indirect investment for the maritime security." These are factors affecting local fishing – one of the country's main national resources – which had a 46% loss in 2008–2009.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-wc-63) International contributions of patrol boats, planes or drones have been provided to help Seychelles combat sea piracy.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-wc-63)

### Administrative divisions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Administrative divisions")]

Main article: [Districts of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Seychelles "Districts of Seychelles")

Seychelles is divided into twenty-six administrative regions comprising all of the inner islands. Eight of the districts make up the capital of Seychelles and are referred to as Greater [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles"). Another 14 districts are considered the rural part of the main island of [Mahé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mah%C3%A9 "Mahé"). Two more districts divide the island of [Praslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praslin "Praslin") and one covers [La Digue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Digue "La Digue") as well as satellite and other [Inner Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles "Granitic Seychelles"). The rest of the [Outer Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Islands_(Seychelles) "Outer Islands (Seychelles)") (_\_Îles Eloignées\__) make up the last district recently created by the tourism ministry.

An island nation, Seychelles is located in the [Somali Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_Sea "Somali Sea") segment of the Indian Ocean, northeast of [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar "Madagascar") and about 1,600 km (860 nmi) east of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). The Constitution of Seychelles lists 155 named islands,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Constitution-64) and a further 7 reclaimed islands have been created subsequent to the publication of the Constitution. The majority of the islands are uninhabited, with many dedicated as nature reserves. Seychelles' largest island, [Mahé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mah%C3%A9 "Mahé"), is located 1,550 km (835 nmi) from [Mogadishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mogadishu "Mogadishu") ([Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia "Somalia")'s capital).[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-65)

Seychelles sits atop a large submerged [granite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granite "Granite") block known as the [Seychelles microcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_microcontinent "Seychelles microcontinent"), which was sandwiched between [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar "Madagascar") and [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") before the breakup of [Gondwanaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondwanaland "Gondwanaland").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Torsvik2013-66)[Alfred Wegener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Wegener "Alfred Wegener") cited the Seychelles' granitic composition, akin to that of continents, as evidence of [continental drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_drift "Continental drift").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-67) After Madagascar separated from India during the [Late Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Cretaceous "Late Cretaceous"), interaction with the [Réunion hotspot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9union_hotspot "Réunion hotspot") caused the diverging oceanic rift to jump several times, breaking off a piece that is currently on the [Somali plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_plate "Somali plate") and includes Seychelles, [Mauritius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritius "Mauritius"), and Réunion, as well as another fragment on the present [Indian plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_plate "Indian plate") that includes [Lakshadweep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshadweep "Lakshadweep"), the [Chagos Archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chagos_Archipelago "Chagos Archipelago"), and the [Maldives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldives "Maldives").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Torsvik2013-66)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-68)

A group of 44 islands (42 granitic and 2 coralline) occupy the shallow waters of the Seychelles Bank and are collectively referred to as the inner islands. They have a total area of 244 km 2 (94 sq mi), accounting for 54% of the total land area of the Seychelles and 98% of the entire population.

The islands have been divided into groups. There are 42 granitic islands known as the [Granitic Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles "Granitic Seychelles"). In addition to these 155 islands, as per the Constitution of Seychelles, there are 7 reclaimed islands: Ile Perseverance, Ile Aurore, [Romainville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romainville_Island,_Seychelles "Romainville Island, Seychelles"), [Eden Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Island,_Seychelles "Eden Island, Seychelles"), Eve, Ile du Port and Ile Soleil.

South Island, African Banks has been eroded by the sea. At St Joseph Atoll, Banc de Sable and Pelican Island have also eroded, while Grand Carcassaye and Petit Carcassaye have merged to form one island. There are also several unnamed islands at Aldabra, St Joseph Atoll and Cosmoledo. Pti Astove, though named, failed to make it into the Constitution for unknown reasons. Bancs Providence is not a single island, but a dynamic group of islands, comprising four large and about six very small islets in 2016.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Climate")]

The climate is very humid, as the islands are small,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-69) and is classified by the [Köppen-Geiger system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen-Geiger_climate_classification_system "Köppen-Geiger climate classification system") as a [tropical rain forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_rainforest_climate "Tropical rainforest climate") (_Af_). The temperature varies little throughout the year. Temperatures on Mahé vary from 24 to 30°C (75 to 86°F), and rainfall ranges from 2,900 mm (114 in) annually at [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles") to 3,600 mm (142 in) on the mountain slopes. [Precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology) "Precipitation (meteorology)") levels are somewhat less on the other islands.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Climate-70)

During the coolest months, July and August, the average low is about 24°C (75°F). The southeast trade winds blow regularly from May to November, and this is the most pleasant time of the year. The hot months are from December to April, with higher humidity (80%). March and April are the hottest months, but the temperature seldom exceeds 31°C (88°F). Most of the islands lie outside the cyclone belt, so high winds are rare.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Climate-70)

Seychelles is among the world's leading countries to protect lands for [threatened species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threatened_species "Threatened species"), allocating 42% of its territory for [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_(ethic) "Conservation (ethic)").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-73) Like many fragile island ecosystems, Seychelles saw the [loss of biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity_loss "Biodiversity loss") when humans first settled in the area, including the disappearance of most of the [giant tortoises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldabrachelys "Aldabrachelys") from the granitic islands, the felling of coastal and mid-level forests, and the extinction of species such as the [chestnut flanked white eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_chestnut-flanked_white-eye "Seychelles chestnut-flanked white-eye"), the [Seychelles parakeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_parakeet "Seychelles parakeet"), and the [saltwater crocodile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saltwater_crocodile "Saltwater crocodile"). However, extinctions were far fewer than on islands such as [Mauritius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritius "Mauritius") or [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii"), partly due to a shorter period of human occupation. Seychelles today is known for success stories in protecting its flora and fauna. The rare [Seychelles black parrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_black_parrot "Seychelles black parrot"), the national bird of the country, is now protected.

The [freshwater crab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_crab "Freshwater crab") genus _[Seychellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellum "Seychellum")_ is endemic to the granitic Seychelles, and a further 26 species of crabs and five species of [hermit crabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermit_crab "Hermit crab") live on the islands.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Haig-74) From the year 1500 until the mid-1800s (approximately), the then-previously unknown [Aldabra giant tortoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldabra_giant_tortoise "Aldabra giant tortoise") was killed for food by pirates and sailors, driving their numbers to near-extinction levels. Today, a healthy yet fragile population of 150,000 tortoises live solely on the atoll of Aldabra, declared a [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")[World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-75)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-76) Additionally, these ancient reptiles can further be found in numerous zoos, botanical gardens, and private collections internationally. Their protection from poaching and smuggling is overseen by [CITES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CITES "CITES"), whilst [captive breeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captive_breeding "Captive breeding") has greatly reduced the negative impact on the remaining wild populations. The granitic islands of Seychelles supports three extant species of [Seychelles giant tortoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_giant_tortoise "Seychelles giant tortoise").

Seychelles hosts some of the largest [seabird colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_colony "Bird colony") in the world, notably on the outer islands of Aldabra and Cosmoledo. In [granitic Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles "Granitic Seychelles") the largest colonies are on [Aride Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aride_Island "Aride Island") including the world's largest numbers of two species. The [sooty tern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sooty_tern "Sooty tern") also breeds on the islands. Other common birds include [cattle egret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattle_egret "Cattle egret") (_Bubulcus ibis_) and the [fairy tern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairy_tern "Fairy tern") (_Gygis alba_).[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-77) More than 1,000 species of fish have been recorded.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The granitic islands of Seychelles are home to roughly 268 [flowering plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiosperms "Angiosperms") species, of which 70 (28%) are endemic.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-78)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-79) Particularly well known is the [coco de mer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_de_mer "Coco de mer"), a species of palm that grows only on the islands of [Praslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praslin "Praslin") and neighbouring [Curieuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curieuse "Curieuse"). Sometimes nicknamed the "love nut" (the shape of its "double" coconut resembles buttocks), the coco-de-mer produces the world's heaviest seed. The [jellyfish tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jellyfish_tree "Jellyfish tree") is to be found in only a few locations on Mahé. This strange and ancient plant, in a genus of its own, _[Medusagyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medusagyne "Medusagyne")_ seems to reproduce only in cultivation and not in the wild. Other unique plant species include Wright's gardenia (_[Rothmannia annae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rothmannia\_annae "Rothmannia annae")_), found only on [Aride Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aride_Island "Aride Island")'s Special Reserve. There are 6 potentially endemic species of orchid living on the islands.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-80)

Seychelles is home to two terrestrial ecoregions: [Granitic Seychelles forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles_forests "Granitic Seychelles forests") and [Aldabra Island xeric scrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldabra_Island_xeric_scrub "Aldabra Island xeric scrub").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-81) The country had a 2019 [Forest Landscape Integrity Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index "Forest Landscape Integrity Index") mean score of 10/10, ranking it first globally out of 172 countries.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-82)

### Environmental issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Environmental issues")]

Since the use of [spearguns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speargun "Speargun") and dynamite for fishing was banned through efforts of local conservationists in the 1960s, the wildlife is unafraid of [snorkelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snorkeling "Snorkeling") and [divers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuba_diving "Scuba diving"). [Coral bleaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_bleaching "Coral bleaching") in 1998 has damaged most reefs, but some reefs show healthy recovery (such as [Silhouette Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silhouette_Island "Silhouette Island")).

Seychelles claims to have achieved nearly all of its [Millennium Development Goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Development_Goals "Millennium Development Goals"), with 7 out of 8 goals having been achieved.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-83) Environmental protection has been emphasized by the government.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-84)

The government's _Seychelles Climate Guide_ describes the nation's climate as rainy, with a dry season with an ocean economy in the ocean regions. The Southeast Trades is on the decline but still fairly strong.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-85) Reportedly, weather patterns there are becoming less predictable.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-86)

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Demographics")]

Main article: [Demographics of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Seychelles "Demographics of Seychelles")

See also: [Indo-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Seychellois "Indo-Seychellois"), [Sino-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Seychellois "Sino-Seychellois"), [Seychellois Creole people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellois_Creole_people "Seychellois Creole people"), [Seychellois Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellois_Creole "Seychellois Creole"), and [Franco-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-Seychellois "Franco-Seychellois")

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Seychelles-Mah%C3%A9-victoria-kevin-gepford.jpg/500px-Seychelles-Mah%C3%A9-victoria-kevin-gepford.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seychelles-Mah%C3%A9-victoria-kevin-gepford.jpg)

[Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles"), capital and largest city of Seychelles

When the British gained control of the islands during the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars"), they allowed the French upper class to retain their land. Both the French and British settlers used enslaved Africans, and although the British prohibited slavery in 1835, African workers continued to come. The _Gran blan_ ("big whites") of French origin dominated economic and political life. The British administration employed Indians on [indentured servitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indentured_servant "Indentured servant") to the same degree as in Mauritius resulting in a small Indian population. The Indians, like a similar minority of Chinese, were generally in the merchant class.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-87)

Today, Seychelles is described as a fusion of peoples and cultures. Numerous Seychellois are considered multiracial: blending from African, Asian and European descent to create a modern creole culture. Evidence of this blend is also revealed in Seychellois food, incorporating various aspects of French, Chinese, Indian and African cuisine.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-88)

As the islands of Seychelles had no indigenous population, the current Seychellois descend from people who immigrated, of which the largest ethnic groups were those of African, French, [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-resident_Indian_and_person_of_Indian_origin "Non-resident Indian and person of Indian origin") and [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Chinese "Overseas Chinese") origin. The [median](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median "Median") age of the Seychellois is 34 years.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-CIA-89)

### Languages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Languages")]

[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language") and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") are official languages along with [Seychellois Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellois_Creole "Seychellois Creole"), which is a [French-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-based_creole "French-based creole")[creole language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creole_language "Creole language") related to those spoken in Mauritius and Réunion. Seychellois [Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creole_language "Creole language") is the most widely spoken native language and de facto the [national language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_language "National language") of the country. Seychellois Creole is often spoken with English words and phrases mixed in.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-ethno-90) About 91% of the population are native speakers of Seychellois Creole, 5.1% of English and 0.7% of French.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-ethno-90) Most business and official meetings are conducted in English and nearly all official websites are in English. National Assembly business is conducted in Creole, but laws are passed and published in English.

[Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") is also a prominent language in Seychelles, spoken primarily by the [Indo-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Seychellois "Indo-Seychellois") community, who form a significant part of the country's multilingual society.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-91)

**Seychelles**[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-11) ([/s eɪ ˈ ʃ ɛ l(z)/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/4/4f/En-us-Seychelles.ogg/En-us-Seychelles.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-Seychelles.ogg "File:En-us-Seychelles.ogg"), [/ˈ s eɪ ʃ ɛ l(z)/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English");[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-12)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-13)French:[[sɛʃɛl]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-14)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-15)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-16)or[[seʃɛl]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-17)), officially the **Republic of Seychelles** (French: _République des Seychelles_; [Seychellois Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellois_Creole "Seychellois Creole"): _Repiblik Sesel_),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-18) is an [archipelagic country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelagic_country "Archipelagic country") consisting of 115 islands[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-19) in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean"). Its capital and largest city, [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles"), is 1,500 kilometres (800 nautical miles) east of mainland [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa"). Nearby island countries and territories include the [Maldives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldives "Maldives"), [Comoros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comoros "Comoros"), [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar "Madagascar"), [Mauritius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritius "Mauritius"), and the [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Fifth_Republic "French Fifth Republic")[overseas departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_departments_and_regions_of_France "Overseas departments and regions of France") of [Mayotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayotte "Mayotte") and [Réunion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9union "Réunion") to the south; and the [Chagos Archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chagos_Archipelago "Chagos Archipelago") to the east. Seychelles is the [smallest country in Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African_countries_by_area "List of African countries by area") as well as the [least populated sovereign African country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African_countries_by_population "List of African countries by population"), with an estimated population of 100,600 in 2022.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-World_Bank_Open_Data_v619-20)

The Seychelles archipelago was uninhabited prior to sustained external contact. Although Arab and Swahili sailors likely knew of the islands earlier through [Indian Ocean trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_trade "Indian Ocean trade") routes, there is no evidence of permanent settlement before European involvement. The islands were first recorded by Europeans in the 16th century, but were not settled until the 18th century, when France formally claimed them. During the period of French colonization, enslaved Africans were brought to the islands for plantation labor; many had already been captured and enslaved through existing African-[Arab slave trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_slave_trade "Arab slave trade") or [Indian Ocean slave trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_slave_trade "Indian Ocean slave trade").

It faced competing French and British interests until it came under full British control in the early 19th century. After Britain assumed control in the early 19th century, slavery was abolished and later replaced in part by indentured laborers from India. Since proclaiming independence from the United Kingdom in 1976, it has developed from a largely [agricultural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture "Agriculture") society to a market-based diversified economy, characterized by [service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_sector "Service sector"), [public sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_sector "Public sector"), and [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism "Tourism") activities. From 1976 to 2015, nominal [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP "GDP") grew nearly 700%, and [purchasing power parity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purchasing_power_parity "Purchasing power parity") nearly 1600%. Since the late 2010s, the government has taken steps to encourage [foreign investment](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/foreign%20investment "wikt:foreign investment").

As of the early 21st century, Seychelles has the highest [nominal per capita GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)_per_capita "List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita") and the highest [Human Development Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index "Human Development Index") ranking of any African country.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-21) According to the 2024 [V-Dem Democracy indices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V-Dem_Democracy_indices "V-Dem Democracy indices"), Seychelles is the 43rd-ranked electoral democracy worldwide, the 1st-ranked [liberal democracy in Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy_in_Africa "Democracy in Africa"), and the 2nd-ranked electoral democracy on the continent.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-vdem_dataset-22) Seychellois culture and society is an eclectic mix of French, British, Indian and African influences, with infusions of Chinese elements. The country is a member of the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union"), the [Southern African Development Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_African_Development_Community "Southern African Development Community"), and the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

Seychelles was uninhabited throughout most of recorded history, although simulations of [Austronesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austronesian_peoples "Austronesian peoples") migration patterns indicate a good probability that they visited the islands.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-23) Tombs visible until 1910 at Anse Lascars on Silhouette Island have also been conjectured to belong to later [Maldivian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldivians "Maldivians") and [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs "Arabs") traders visiting the archipelago.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-24)[Vasco da Gama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama "Vasco da Gama") and his [4th Portuguese India Armada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_Portuguese_India_Armada_(Gama,_1502) "4th Portuguese India Armada (Gama, 1502)") discovered the Seychelles on 15 March 1503; the first sighting was made by [Thomé Lopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thom%C3%A9_Lopes "Thomé Lopes") aboard _Rui Mendes de Brito_. Da Gama's ships passed close to an elevated island, probably [Silhouette Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silhouette_Island "Silhouette Island"), and the following day [Desroches Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desroches_Island "Desroches Island"). Later, the Portuguese mapped a group of seven islands and named them _The Seven Sisters._[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-25) The earliest recorded landing was in January 1609, by the crew of the _Ascension_ under Captain [Alexander Sharpeigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Sharpeigh "Alexander Sharpeigh") during the fourth voyage of the British [East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company "East India Company").

A transit point for trade between Africa and Asia, the islands were said to be occasionally used by pirates until the French began to take control in 1756 when a Stone of Possession was laid on [Mahé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mah%C3%A9 "Mahé") by Captain [Corneille Nicholas Morphey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneille_Nicholas_Morphey "Corneille Nicholas Morphey"). The islands were named after French politician [Jean Moreau de Séchelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Moreau_de_S%C3%A9chelles "Jean Moreau de Séchelles"), and were formally part of the colony of [Isle de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_de_France_(Mauritius) "Isle de France (Mauritius)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-26) In August 1770, the French ship _Thélémaque_ under Captain Leblanc Lécore landed 15 white settlers and 13 African and Indian slaves on [Ste. Anne Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ste._Anne_Island "Ste. Anne Island").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-27)

During the [French Revolutionary Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Wars "French Revolutionary Wars"), the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") frigate [HMS _Orpheus_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Orpheus_(1780) "HMS Orpheus (1780)") under Captain Henry Newcombe arrived at Mahé on 16 May 1794. [Jean-Baptiste Quéau de Quinssy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Baptiste_Qu%C3%A9au_de_Quinssy?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jean-Baptiste Quéau de Quinssy (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Baptiste%20Qu%C3%A9au%20de%20Quinssy "fr:Jean-Baptiste Quéau de Quinssy")], the senior administrator in the Seychelles, refused to resist _Orpheus_ and instead successfully negotiated with the British, resulting the islands remaining under French control as "neutral" territory. After British forces completed their [invasion of Isle de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Isle_de_France "Invasion of Isle de France") in December 1810, they assumed control over the Seychelles, which was formalised in the 1814 [Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1814) "Treaty of Paris (1814)") that ended the [War of the Sixth Coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Sixth_Coalition "War of the Sixth Coalition"). Seychelles became a separate [crown colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_colony "Crown colony") from Mauritius in 1903. [Elections in Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elections_in_Seychelles "Elections in Seychelles") were held in 1966 and 1970.

### Independence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Independence")]

In 1976, Seychelles gained independence from the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") as a republic. It has since become a member of the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-History_of_Seychelles-28) In the 1970s Seychelles was "the place to be seen, a playground for film stars and the international jet set".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29) In 1977, a [coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Seychelles_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1977 Seychelles coup d'état") by [France-Albert René](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France-Albert_Ren%C3%A9 "France-Albert René") ousted the first president of the republic, [James Mancham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Mancham "James Mancham").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-africanhistory.about.com-30) René discouraged over-dependence on tourism and declared that he wanted "to keep Seychelles for the Seychellois".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29)

The 1979 constitution declared a [socialist one-party state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_party_rule_in_Seychelles "One party rule in Seychelles"), which lasted until 1991.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-31)

In the 1980s there were a series of coup attempts against President René, some of which were supported by South Africa. In 1981, [Mike Hoare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Hoare "Mike Hoare") led a team of 43 South African mercenaries masquerading as holidaying rugby players in the [1981 Seychelles coup d'état attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Seychelles_coup_d'%C3%A9tat_attempt "1981 Seychelles coup d'état attempt").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29) There was a gun battle at the airport, and most of the mercenaries later escaped in a hijacked [Air India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_India "Air India") plane.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-29) The leader of this hijacking was German mercenary D. Clodo, a former member of the [Rhodesian SAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodesian_Special_Air_Service "Rhodesian Special Air Service").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-32) Clodo later stood trial in South Africa (where he was acquitted) as well as in his home country Germany for air piracy.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-33)

In 1986, an attempted coup led by the Seychelles Minister of Defence, Ogilvy Berlouis, caused President René to request assistance from India. In [Operation Flowers are Blooming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Flowers_are_Blooming "Operation Flowers are Blooming"), the Indian Navy's [_Nilgiri_-class frigate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilgiri-class_frigate_(1972) "Nilgiri-class frigate (1972)")[_Vindhyagiri_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Vindhyagiri_(F42) "INS Vindhyagiri (F42)") arrived in Port Victoria to help avert the coup.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-34)

The first draft of a new constitution failed to receive the requisite 60% of voters in 1992, but an amended version was approved in 1993.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-35)

In January 2013, Seychelles declared a state of emergency when the tropical [cyclone Felleng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Felleng "Cyclone Felleng") caused torrential rain, and flooding and landslides destroyed hundreds of houses.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-UN-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-AL-37)

Following the coup in 1977, the president always represented the same political party until the October [2020 Seychellois general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Seychellois_general_election "2020 Seychellois general election"), which was historic in that the opposition party won. [Wavel Ramkalawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavel_Ramkalawan "Wavel Ramkalawan") was the first president who did not represent United Seychelles (the current name of the former Seychelles People's Progressive Front).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-38)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-39)

In January 2023, Seychelles announced its final stages of completing its marine spatial plan. It would become the second largest ocean area at 1.35 million km 2 (520,000 sq mi) behind [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway"), in support of its [blue economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_economy "Blue economy").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-40)

In October 2025, [presidential runoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Seychellois_general_election "2025 Seychellois general election") was won by former parliamentary speaker and main opposition leader, [Patrick Herminie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Herminie "Patrick Herminie"), meaning Herminie's party, [United Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Seychelles "United Seychelles") (US) returned to power.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-41) On 26 October 2025, Patrick Herminie was sworn in as Seychelles' sixth president.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-reuters.com-42)

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Politics")]

Main article: [Politics of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Seychelles "Politics of Seychelles")

The Seychelles president, who is [head of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state") and [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government"), is elected by popular vote for a five-year term of office. The cabinet is presided over and appointed by the president, subject to the approval of a majority of the legislature. As of 2026, the president is [Patrick Herminie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Herminie "Patrick Herminie").

The [unicameral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicameral "Unicameral") Seychellois parliament, the [National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_(Seychelles) "National Assembly (Seychelles)") or _Assemblée Nationale_, consists of 35 members, 26 of whom are elected directly by popular vote, while the remaining nine seats are appointed proportionally according to the percentage of votes received by each party. All members serve five-year terms.

The [Supreme Court of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Seychelles "Supreme Court of Seychelles"), created in 1903, is the highest trial court in Seychelles and the first court of appeal from all the lower courts and tribunals. The highest court of law in Seychelles is the Seychelles Court of Appeal, which is the court of final appeal in the country.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-43)

### Political culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Political culture")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/James_Michel_in_meeting.jpg/250px-James_Michel_in_meeting.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Michel_in_meeting.jpg)

President [James Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Michel "James Michel") in his office in [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles"), 2009

Seychelles' long-term president [France-Albert René](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France-Albert_Ren%C3%A9 "France-Albert René") came to power after his supporters overthrew the first president [James Mancham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Mancham "James Mancham") on 5 June 1977 in a [coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_d'%C3%A9tat "Coup d'état") and installed him as president. René was at that time the prime minister. René ruled as a [strongman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strongman_(politics) "Strongman (politics)") under a [socialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist "Socialist")[one-party system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-party_system "One-party system") until 1993, when he was forced to introduce a multi-party system. He stepped down in 2004 in favour of his vice-president, [James Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Michel "James Michel"), who was re-elected in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Seychellois_presidential_election "2006 Seychellois presidential election"), [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Seychellois_presidential_election "2011 Seychellois presidential election") and again in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Seychellois_presidential_election "2015 Seychellois presidential election").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-44)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Seychelles_Nation-45)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Reuters-46)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Agence_France-Presse-47) On 28 September 2016, the Office of the President announced that Michel would step down effective 16 October, and that Vice President [Danny Faure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Faure "Danny Faure") would complete the rest of Michel's term.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-48)

On 26 October 2020, [Wavel Ramkalawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavel_Ramkalawan "Wavel Ramkalawan"), a 59-year-old Anglican priest, was elected the fifth President of the Republic of Seychelles. Ramkalawan was an opposition MP from 1993 to 2011, and from 2016 to 2020. He served as the [Leader of the Opposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Opposition_(Seychelles) "Leader of the Opposition (Seychelles)") from 1998 to 2011 and from 2016 to 2020. Ramkalawan defeated incumbent Danny Faure by 54.9% to 43.5%. This marked the first time the opposition had won a presidential election in Seychelles.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-49)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-50)

The primary political parties are the former long-time ruling socialist [People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Party_(Seychelles) "People's Party (Seychelles)") (PP), known until 2009 as the Seychelles People's Progressive Front (SPPF) now called [United Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Seychelles "United Seychelles") (US), and the [socially liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_liberalism "Social liberalism")[Seychelles National Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_National_Party "Seychelles National Party") (SNP).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-51)

The [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Seychellois_general_election "2020 Seychellois general election") of the National Assembly was held on 22–24 October 2020. The Seychelles National Party, the Seychelles Party for Social Justice and Democracy and the Seychelles United Party formed a coalition, [Linyon Demokratik Seselwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linyon_Demokratik_Seselwa "Linyon Demokratik Seselwa") (LDS). LDS won 25 seats and US got 10 seats of the 35 seats of the National Assembly.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-52) However, in the 2025 Seychellois general [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Seychellois_general_election "2025 Seychellois general election") United Seychelles won 15 out of 26 seats in the parliament.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-53)

### Foreign relations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Foreign relations")]

Further information: [Foreign relations of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Seychelles "Foreign relations of Seychelles")

Seychelles is a member of the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union"), the [Indian Ocean Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_Commission "Indian Ocean Commission"), [La Francophonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Francophonie "La Francophonie"), the [Southern African Development Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_African_Development_Community "Southern African Development Community") and the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").

Between 1979 and 1983, various plots to overthrow the non-aligned government of France-Albert René were, according to leading participants, supported by the United States, France, and South Africa. Commonly cited reasons for such attempts include René's socialist politics, his non-aligned stance toward the Western and Eastern Blocs, and the United States' military lease in the country, which was set to expire in 1990. All coup efforts in this period failed.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-54) Under the Obama administration, the US began running drone operations out of Seychelles.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-:0-55) In the Spring of 2013, members of the [Special-Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Purpose_Marine_Air-Ground_Task_Force_%E2%80%93_Crisis_Response_%E2%80%93_Africa "Special Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force – Crisis Response – Africa") mentored troops in Seychelles, along with a variety of other African nations.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-:0-55)

### Military

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Military")]

Main article: [Seychelles People's Defence Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_People's_Defence_Force "Seychelles People's Defence Force")

The [military of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_Seychelles "Military of Seychelles") is the [Seychelles People's Defence Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_People's_Defence_Force "Seychelles People's Defence Force") which consists of a number of distinct branches: an infantry unit and coast guard, air force and a presidential protection unit. India has played and continues to play a key role in developing the military of Seychelles. After handing over two [SDB Mk5 patrol vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinkat-class_patrol_vessel "Trinkat-class patrol vessel") built by [GRSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GRSE "GRSE"), the INS _Tarasa_ and INS _Tarmugli_, to the [Seychelles Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_Coast_Guard "Seychelles Coast Guard"), which were subsequently renamed [PS _Constant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PS_Constant "PS Constant") and [PS _Topaz_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PS_Topaz "PS Topaz"), India also gifted a [Dornier 228](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dornier_228 "Dornier 228") aircraft built by [Hindustan Aeronautics Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan_Aeronautics_Limited "Hindustan Aeronautics Limited").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-56) India also signed a pact to develop [Assumption Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Island "Assumption Island"). Spread over 11 km 2 (4 sq mi), it is strategically located in the [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean"), north of [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar "Madagascar"). The island is being leased for the development of strategic assets by India.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-57) In 2018, Seychelles signed the UN [Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_on_the_Prohibition_of_Nuclear_Weapons "Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-58)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-59)

### Incarceration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Incarceration")]

Further information: [List of countries by incarceration rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_incarceration_rate "List of countries by incarceration rate")

In 2014, Seychelles had the highest incarceration rate in the world of 799 prisoners per 100,000 population, exceeding the United States' rate by 15%.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-60) However, the country's actual population was less than 100,000; as of September 2014, Seychelles had 735 actual prisoners, 6% of whom were female and were incarcerated in three prisons.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-61)

The incarceration rate in Seychelles has since dropped significantly. It is no longer among the top ten countries with the highest rate of incarceration. In 2022, the incarceration rate was 287 per 100,000 population, being just the 31st highest in the world.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-62)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

### Modern piracy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Modern piracy")]

Seychelles is a key participant in the fight against Indian Ocean [piracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracy "Piracy") primarily committed by [Somali pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracy_off_the_coast_of_Somalia#Effects_and_perceptions "Piracy off the coast of Somalia").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-wc-63) Former president [James Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Michel "James Michel") said that piracy costs between $7 million – $12 million a year to the international community: "The pirates cost 4% of the Seychelles [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product"), including direct and indirect costs for the loss of boats, fishing, and tourism, and the indirect investment for the maritime security." These are factors affecting local fishing – one of the country's main national resources – which had a 46% loss in 2008–2009.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-wc-63) International contributions of patrol boats, planes or drones have been provided to help Seychelles combat sea piracy.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-wc-63)

### Administrative divisions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Administrative divisions")]

Main article: [Districts of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Seychelles "Districts of Seychelles")

Seychelles is divided into twenty-six administrative regions comprising all of the inner islands. Eight of the districts make up the capital of Seychelles and are referred to as Greater [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles"). Another 14 districts are considered the rural part of the main island of [Mahé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mah%C3%A9 "Mahé"). Two more districts divide the island of [Praslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praslin "Praslin") and one covers [La Digue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Digue "La Digue") as well as satellite and other [Inner Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles "Granitic Seychelles"). The rest of the [Outer Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Islands_(Seychelles) "Outer Islands (Seychelles)") (_\_Îles Eloignées\__) make up the last district recently created by the tourism ministry.

An island nation, Seychelles is located in the [Somali Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_Sea "Somali Sea") segment of the Indian Ocean, northeast of [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar "Madagascar") and about 1,600 km (860 nmi) east of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). The Constitution of Seychelles lists 155 named islands,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Constitution-64) and a further 7 reclaimed islands have been created subsequent to the publication of the Constitution. The majority of the islands are uninhabited, with many dedicated as nature reserves. Seychelles' largest island, [Mahé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mah%C3%A9 "Mahé"), is located 1,550 km (835 nmi) from [Mogadishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mogadishu "Mogadishu") ([Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia "Somalia")'s capital).[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-65)

Seychelles sits atop a large submerged [granite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granite "Granite") block known as the [Seychelles microcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_microcontinent "Seychelles microcontinent"), which was sandwiched between [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar "Madagascar") and [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") before the breakup of [Gondwanaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondwanaland "Gondwanaland").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Torsvik2013-66)[Alfred Wegener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Wegener "Alfred Wegener") cited the Seychelles' granitic composition, akin to that of continents, as evidence of [continental drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_drift "Continental drift").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-67) After Madagascar separated from India during the [Late Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Cretaceous "Late Cretaceous"), interaction with the [Réunion hotspot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9union_hotspot "Réunion hotspot") caused the diverging oceanic rift to jump several times, breaking off a piece that is currently on the [Somali plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_plate "Somali plate") and includes Seychelles, [Mauritius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritius "Mauritius"), and Réunion, as well as another fragment on the present [Indian plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_plate "Indian plate") that includes [Lakshadweep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshadweep "Lakshadweep"), the [Chagos Archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chagos_Archipelago "Chagos Archipelago"), and the [Maldives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maldives "Maldives").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Torsvik2013-66)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-68)

A group of 44 islands (42 granitic and 2 coralline) occupy the shallow waters of the Seychelles Bank and are collectively referred to as the inner islands. They have a total area of 244 km 2 (94 sq mi), accounting for 54% of the total land area of the Seychelles and 98% of the entire population.

The islands have been divided into groups. There are 42 granitic islands known as the [Granitic Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles "Granitic Seychelles"). Anne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ste._Anne_Island "Ste. There are 13 coral islands in the [Farquhar Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farquhar_Group "Farquhar Group"), south-southwest of the Amirantes: [Farquhar Atoll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farquhar_Atoll "Farquhar Atoll") (comprising 10 islands—Bancs de Sable, Déposés, Île aux Goëlettes, Lapins, Île du Milieu, North Manaha, South Manaha, Middle Manaha, North Island and South Island), Providence Atoll (comprising two islands—Providence and Bancs Providence) and St Pierre.
