In addition to these 155 islands, as per the Constitution of Seychelles, there are 7 reclaimed islands: Ile Perseverance, Ile Aurore, [Romainville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romainville_Island,_Seychelles "Romainville Island, Seychelles"), [Eden Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Island,_Seychelles "Eden Island, Seychelles"), Eve, Ile du Port and Ile Soleil.

South Island, African Banks has been eroded by the sea. At St Joseph Atoll, Banc de Sable and Pelican Island have also eroded, while Grand Carcassaye and Petit Carcassaye have merged to form one island. There are also several unnamed islands at Aldabra, St Joseph Atoll and Cosmoledo. Pti Astove, though named, failed to make it into the Constitution for unknown reasons. Bancs Providence is not a single island, but a dynamic group of islands, comprising four large and about six very small islets in 2016.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Climate")]

The climate is very humid, as the islands are small,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-69) and is classified by the [Köppen-Geiger system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen-Geiger_climate_classification_system "Köppen-Geiger climate classification system") as a [tropical rain forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_rainforest_climate "Tropical rainforest climate") (_Af_). The temperature varies little throughout the year. Temperatures on Mahé vary from 24 to 30°C (75 to 86°F), and rainfall ranges from 2,900 mm (114 in) annually at [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles") to 3,600 mm (142 in) on the mountain slopes. [Precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology) "Precipitation (meteorology)") levels are somewhat less on the other islands.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Climate-70)

During the coolest months, July and August, the average low is about 24°C (75°F). The southeast trade winds blow regularly from May to November, and this is the most pleasant time of the year. The hot months are from December to April, with higher humidity (80%). March and April are the hottest months, but the temperature seldom exceeds 31°C (88°F). Most of the islands lie outside the cyclone belt, so high winds are rare.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Climate-70)

### Wildlife

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Wildlife")]

Main article: [Wildlife of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildlife_of_Seychelles "Wildlife of Seychelles")

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Seychelles_Paradise-flycatcher.jpg/120px-Seychelles_Paradise-flycatcher.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seychelles_Paradise-flycatcher.jpg)

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Bird_flocks_Bird_Island_Seychelles.jpg/250px-Bird_flocks_Bird_Island_Seychelles.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bird_flocks_Bird_Island_Seychelles.jpg)

Left: [Seychelles paradise flycatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_paradise_flycatcher "Seychelles paradise flycatcher"); right: bird flocks on [Bird Island, Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_Island,_Seychelles "Bird Island, Seychelles")

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Aldabra_Female_on_Curieuse.JPG/250px-Aldabra_Female_on_Curieuse.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aldabra_Female_on_Curieuse.JPG)

An [Aldabra giant tortoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldabra_giant_tortoise "Aldabra giant tortoise")

Seychelles is among the world's leading countries to protect lands for [threatened species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threatened_species "Threatened species"), allocating 42% of its territory for [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_(ethic) "Conservation (ethic)").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-73) Like many fragile island ecosystems, Seychelles saw the [loss of biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity_loss "Biodiversity loss") when humans first settled in the area, including the disappearance of most of the [giant tortoises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldabrachelys "Aldabrachelys") from the granitic islands, the felling of coastal and mid-level forests, and the extinction of species such as the [chestnut flanked white eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_chestnut-flanked_white-eye "Seychelles chestnut-flanked white-eye"), the [Seychelles parakeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_parakeet "Seychelles parakeet"), and the [saltwater crocodile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saltwater_crocodile "Saltwater crocodile"). However, extinctions were far fewer than on islands such as [Mauritius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritius "Mauritius") or [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii"), partly due to a shorter period of human occupation. Seychelles today is known for success stories in protecting its flora and fauna. The rare [Seychelles black parrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_black_parrot "Seychelles black parrot"), the national bird of the country, is now protected.

The [freshwater crab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_crab "Freshwater crab") genus _[Seychellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellum "Seychellum")_ is endemic to the granitic Seychelles, and a further 26 species of crabs and five species of [hermit crabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermit_crab "Hermit crab") live on the islands.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-Haig-74) From the year 1500 until the mid-1800s (approximately), the then-previously unknown [Aldabra giant tortoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldabra_giant_tortoise "Aldabra giant tortoise") was killed for food by pirates and sailors, driving their numbers to near-extinction levels. Today, a healthy yet fragile population of 150,000 tortoises live solely on the atoll of Aldabra, declared a [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")[World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-75)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-76) Additionally, these ancient reptiles can further be found in numerous zoos, botanical gardens, and private collections internationally. Their protection from poaching and smuggling is overseen by [CITES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CITES "CITES"), whilst [captive breeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captive_breeding "Captive breeding") has greatly reduced the negative impact on the remaining wild populations. The granitic islands of Seychelles supports three extant species of [Seychelles giant tortoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles_giant_tortoise "Seychelles giant tortoise").

Seychelles hosts some of the largest [seabird colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_colony "Bird colony") in the world, notably on the outer islands of Aldabra and Cosmoledo. In [granitic Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles "Granitic Seychelles") the largest colonies are on [Aride Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aride_Island "Aride Island") including the world's largest numbers of two species. The [sooty tern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sooty_tern "Sooty tern") also breeds on the islands. Other common birds include [cattle egret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattle_egret "Cattle egret") (_Bubulcus ibis_) and the [fairy tern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairy_tern "Fairy tern") (_Gygis alba_).[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-77) More than 1,000 species of fish have been recorded.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The granitic islands of Seychelles are home to roughly 268 [flowering plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiosperms "Angiosperms") species, of which 70 (28%) are endemic.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-78)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-79) Particularly well known is the [coco de mer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coco_de_mer "Coco de mer"), a species of palm that grows only on the islands of [Praslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praslin "Praslin") and neighbouring [Curieuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curieuse "Curieuse"). Sometimes nicknamed the "love nut" (the shape of its "double" coconut resembles buttocks), the coco-de-mer produces the world's heaviest seed. The [jellyfish tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jellyfish_tree "Jellyfish tree") is to be found in only a few locations on Mahé. This strange and ancient plant, in a genus of its own, _[Medusagyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medusagyne "Medusagyne")_ seems to reproduce only in cultivation and not in the wild. Other unique plant species include Wright's gardenia (_[Rothmannia annae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rothmannia\_annae "Rothmannia annae")_), found only on [Aride Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aride_Island "Aride Island")'s Special Reserve. There are 6 potentially endemic species of orchid living on the islands.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-80)

Seychelles is home to two terrestrial ecoregions: [Granitic Seychelles forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granitic_Seychelles_forests "Granitic Seychelles forests") and [Aldabra Island xeric scrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldabra_Island_xeric_scrub "Aldabra Island xeric scrub").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-81) The country had a 2019 [Forest Landscape Integrity Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index "Forest Landscape Integrity Index") mean score of 10/10, ranking it first globally out of 172 countries.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-82)

### Environmental issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Environmental issues")]

Since the use of [spearguns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speargun "Speargun") and dynamite for fishing was banned through efforts of local conservationists in the 1960s, the wildlife is unafraid of [snorkelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snorkeling "Snorkeling") and [divers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuba_diving "Scuba diving"). [Coral bleaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_bleaching "Coral bleaching") in 1998 has damaged most reefs, but some reefs show healthy recovery (such as [Silhouette Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silhouette_Island "Silhouette Island")).

Seychelles claims to have achieved nearly all of its [Millennium Development Goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Development_Goals "Millennium Development Goals"), with 7 out of 8 goals having been achieved.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-83) Environmental protection has been emphasized by the government.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-84)

The government's _Seychelles Climate Guide_ describes the nation's climate as rainy, with a dry season with an ocean economy in the ocean regions. The Southeast Trades is on the decline but still fairly strong.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-85) Reportedly, weather patterns there are becoming less predictable.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-86)

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Demographics")]

Main article: [Demographics of Seychelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Seychelles "Demographics of Seychelles")

See also: [Indo-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Seychellois "Indo-Seychellois"), [Sino-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Seychellois "Sino-Seychellois"), [Seychellois Creole people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellois_Creole_people "Seychellois Creole people"), [Seychellois Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellois_Creole "Seychellois Creole"), and [Franco-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-Seychellois "Franco-Seychellois")

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Seychelles-Mah%C3%A9-victoria-kevin-gepford.jpg/500px-Seychelles-Mah%C3%A9-victoria-kevin-gepford.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seychelles-Mah%C3%A9-victoria-kevin-gepford.jpg)

[Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Seychelles "Victoria, Seychelles"), capital and largest city of Seychelles

When the British gained control of the islands during the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars"), they allowed the French upper class to retain their land. Both the French and British settlers used enslaved Africans, and although the British prohibited slavery in 1835, African workers continued to come. The _Gran blan_ ("big whites") of French origin dominated economic and political life. The British administration employed Indians on [indentured servitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indentured_servant "Indentured servant") to the same degree as in Mauritius resulting in a small Indian population. The Indians, like a similar minority of Chinese, were generally in the merchant class.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-87)

Today, Seychelles is described as a fusion of peoples and cultures. Numerous Seychellois are considered multiracial: blending from African, Asian and European descent to create a modern creole culture. Evidence of this blend is also revealed in Seychellois food, incorporating various aspects of French, Chinese, Indian and African cuisine.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-88)

As the islands of Seychelles had no indigenous population, the current Seychellois descend from people who immigrated, of which the largest ethnic groups were those of African, French, [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-resident_Indian_and_person_of_Indian_origin "Non-resident Indian and person of Indian origin") and [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Chinese "Overseas Chinese") origin. The [median](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median "Median") age of the Seychellois is 34 years.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-CIA-89)

### Languages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seychelles&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Languages")]

[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language") and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") are official languages along with [Seychellois Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychellois_Creole "Seychellois Creole"), which is a [French-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-based_creole "French-based creole")[creole language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creole_language "Creole language") related to those spoken in Mauritius and Réunion. Seychellois [Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creole_language "Creole language") is the most widely spoken native language and de facto the [national language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_language "National language") of the country. Seychellois Creole is often spoken with English words and phrases mixed in.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-ethno-90) About 91% of the population are native speakers of Seychellois Creole, 5.1% of English and 0.7% of French.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-ethno-90) Most business and official meetings are conducted in English and nearly all official websites are in English. National Assembly business is conducted in Creole, but laws are passed and published in English.

[Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_language "Tamil language") is also a prominent language in Seychelles, spoken primarily by the [Indo-Seychellois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Seychellois "Indo-Seychellois") community, who form a significant part of the country's multilingual society.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seychelles#cite_note-91)

**Dame Sandra Prunella Mason**[FB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Freedom_of_Barbados "Order of Freedom of Barbados")[GCMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St_Michael_and_St_George "Order of St Michael and St George")[DA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_or_Dame_of_St_Andrew "Knight or Dame of St Andrew")[SC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Counsel "Senior Counsel") (born 17 January 1949) is a Barbadian politician, lawyer, and diplomat who served as the first [president of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Barbados "President of Barbados") from 2021 to 2025. She was previously the eighth and final [governor-general of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-general_of_Barbados "Governor-general of Barbados") from 2018 to 2021, the second woman to hold the office. On 20 October 2021, Mason was [elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Barbadian_presidential_election "2021 Barbadian presidential election") by the [Parliament of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Barbados "Parliament of Barbados") to become the country's first president, and took office on 30 November 2021, when Barbados ceased to be a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Barbados "Monarchy of Barbados") and [became a republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_Barbados "Republicanism in Barbados").

Mason was a practising [attorney-at-law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney-at-law "Attorney-at-law") who has served as a High Court [judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judge "Judge") in [Saint Lucia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucia "Saint Lucia") and a Court of Appeal judge in Barbados, and was the first woman admitted to the [bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_(law) "Bar (law)") in Barbados. She served as chair of the [CARICOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARICOM "CARICOM") commission to evaluate regional integration, was the first magistrate appointed an [ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambassador "Ambassador") from Barbados, and was the first woman to serve on the country's [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_Supreme_Court "Barbados Supreme Court"). She was the first appointee from Barbados to the Commonwealth Secretariat Arbitral Tribunal. In 2017, she was appointed the 8th governor-general of Barbados, with a term beginning on 8 January 2018. Simultaneously with her appointment, Mason was awarded the Dame Grand Cross in the [Order of Saint Michael and Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Saint_Michael_and_Saint_George "Order of Saint Michael and Saint George"). On assumption of the office of Governor-General, she became the Chancellor of the [Order of National Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_National_Heroes "Order of National Heroes"), [Order of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Barbados "Order of Barbados") and the [Order of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Freedom_of_Barbados "Order of Freedom of Barbados").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Sandra Prunella Mason was born on 17 January 1949[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) in [Saint Philip, Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Philip,_Barbados "Saint Philip, Barbados").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-(CSAT)-4) After studying at St. Catherine's Primary School until age nine, she attended secondary school at [Queen's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_College_(Barbados) "Queen's College (Barbados)"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-BarbadosGov-5) then began teaching at the Princess Margaret Secondary School in 1968.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-6) The following year, she worked at [Barclays Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Bank "Barclays Bank") as a clerk. Mason enrolled in the [University of the West Indies at Cave Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_West_Indies_at_Cave_Hill "University of the West Indies at Cave Hill"), where she earned a [Bachelor of Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Laws "Bachelor of Laws").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) Mason was one of the first graduates of the Faculty of Law from UWI, Cave Hill, completing her education in 1973.

In 1975, she obtained a [Legal Education Certificate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_Education_Certificate "Legal Education Certificate") from [Hugh Wooding Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Wooding_Law_School "Hugh Wooding Law School") in [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago "Trinidad and Tobago"), becoming the first woman attorney-at-law from Barbados to graduate from the school.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-BarbadosGov-5) She was [admitted to the bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admitted_to_the_bar "Admitted to the bar") on 10 November the same year,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrathwaite1999287-7) becoming the first woman member of the Barbados Bar Association.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) She is a [Soroptimist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soroptimist_International "Soroptimist International") and Patron of SI Barbados.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-8)

## Early career and legal practice

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career and legal practice")]

Beginning in 1975, she worked in Trust Administration for Barclay's and transferred to several different posts within the Barclay's company until 1977.

In 1978, Mason began working as the Magistrate of the Juvenile and Family Court and simultaneously tutoring in family law at UWI. She stopped tutoring in 1983 and continued working as a magistrate. In 1988, Mason completed the [Royal Institute of Public Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_Public_Administration "Royal Institute of Public Administration") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")'s course on Judicial Administration.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) She served on the UN [Committee on the Rights of the Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_on_the_Rights_of_the_Child "Committee on the Rights of the Child") from its 1991 inception until 1999, holding the vice chair from 1993 to 1995 and chair from 1997 to 1999.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEricksonCohenHart2001231-9)

Between 1991 and 1992, Mason served as chair[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) and was one of the two women appointed to the 13-member [CARICOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARICOM "CARICOM") commission charged with evaluating regional integration.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-(CSAT)-4) She left the family court in 1992[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) to serve as an ambassador to Venezuela, and was the first woman magistrate from Barbados to serve in that position. Between 1993 and 1994 she also served as ambassador to [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"), [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") and [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-BarbadosGov-5) Upon her return to Barbados[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrathwaite1999287-7) in 1994, Mason was appointed Chief Magistrate for Barbados, and in 1997 became the Registrar of the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Barbados "Supreme Court of Barbados").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-appellate_judge-10)

In 2000, Mason completed studies on Alternative Dispute Resolution at the [University of Windsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Windsor_Faculty_of_Law "University of Windsor Faculty of Law") in [Windsor, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor,_Ontario "Windsor, Ontario"), Canada, and then completed a Fellowship with the [Commonwealth Judicial Education Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Judicial_Education_Institute?action=edit&redlink=1 "Commonwealth Judicial Education Institute (page does not exist)") in [Halifax, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax,_Nova_Scotia "Halifax, Nova Scotia"), in 2001, as well as a course in Advanced Dispute Resolution at UWI.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) She continued to serve as Registrar of the Supreme Court until 2005, when she was appointed as Queen's Counsel to the Inner Bar of Barbados.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) In 2008, Mason was sworn in as an Appeals Judge[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-appellate_judge-10) becoming the first woman to serve on the Barbados Court of Appeals.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) For three days in 2012, she became the acting Governor-General of Barbados[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Acting_GG-11) and the following year was the first Barbadian appointed to membership in the [Commonwealth Secretariat Arbitral Tribunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Secretariat_Arbitral_Tribunal "Commonwealth Secretariat Arbitral Tribunal") (CSAT). The Tribunal operates among members of the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") to resolve issues concerning contract disputes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-(CSAT)-4) With that appointment, _Loop News_ named her one of the 10 most powerful women in Barbados.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-10_most_powerful-12)

## Governor-General of Barbados

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Governor-General of Barbados")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/2020_Independence_Day_Parade_and_National_Awards_Ceremony_%2850665847882%29.jpg/250px-2020_Independence_Day_Parade_and_National_Awards_Ceremony_%2850665847882%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2020_Independence_Day_Parade_and_National_Awards_Ceremony_(50665847882).jpg)

Mason presenting National Awards during the 2020 Independence Day parade

In 2017, Mason was appointed as the eighth Governor-General of Barbados, with a term beginning on 8 January 2018. Simultaneously with her appointment, Mason was also appointed a Dame Grand Cross in the [Order of Saint Michael and Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Saint_Michael_and_Saint_George "Order of Saint Michael and Saint George").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-13)

In 2020, Mason, in her official capacity announcing government policy in the [Throne Speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throne_Speech "Throne Speech"), written by the government of Prime Minister [Mia Mottley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_Mottley "Mia Mottley"), stated that [Barbados would become a republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_Barbados "Republicanism in Barbados"), abolishing the [Barbadian monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Barbados "Monarchy of Barbados").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-14) She was then expected to be nominated as a candidate to be the first president of Barbados, then to be elected by the two houses of parliament, and to assume office on 30 November 2021.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-17)

## President of Barbados

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: President of Barbados")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Barbados_Independence_Republic_Night_%2851717663162%29.jpg/250px-Barbados_Independence_Republic_Night_%2851717663162%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barbados_Independence_Republic_Night_(51717663162).jpg)

Mason taking oath as the first president of Barbados, 2021

On 12 October 2021, Mason was nominated by Prime Minister [Mia Mottley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_Mottley "Mia Mottley") and Opposition Leader [Joseph Atherley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Atherley "Joseph Atherley") to become the first [president of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Barbados "President of Barbados").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-18) On 20 October she was [elected by both houses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Barbadian_presidential_election "2021 Barbadian presidential election") without opposition.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-19) Mason took office on 30 November 2021,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-:0-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-21) the 55th anniversary of [Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_Independence_Act_1966 "Barbados Independence Act 1966"). While she is nominally chief executive and is the sole head of state in Barbados, in practice her role is mostly ceremonial, much like her previous role as Governor-General.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-22) She made her first official visit to [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") in June 2022.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-23)

As president, Mason represented Barbados at the [state funeral of Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_funeral_of_Queen_Elizabeth_II "State funeral of Queen Elizabeth II") in 2022, and at the [coronation of King Charles III and Queen Camilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation_of_King_Charles_III_and_Queen_Camilla "Coronation of King Charles III and Queen Camilla") in 2023.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-25)

**Dame Sandra Prunella Mason**[FB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Freedom_of_Barbados "Order of Freedom of Barbados")[GCMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St_Michael_and_St_George "Order of St Michael and St George")[DA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_or_Dame_of_St_Andrew "Knight or Dame of St Andrew")[SC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Counsel "Senior Counsel") (born 17 January 1949) is a Barbadian politician, lawyer, and diplomat who served as the first [president of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Barbados "President of Barbados") from 2021 to 2025. She was previously the eighth and final [governor-general of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-general_of_Barbados "Governor-general of Barbados") from 2018 to 2021, the second woman to hold the office. On 20 October 2021, Mason was [elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Barbadian_presidential_election "2021 Barbadian presidential election") by the [Parliament of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Barbados "Parliament of Barbados") to become the country's first president, and took office on 30 November 2021, when Barbados ceased to be a [constitutional monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Barbados "Monarchy of Barbados") and [became a republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_Barbados "Republicanism in Barbados").

Mason was a practising [attorney-at-law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney-at-law "Attorney-at-law") who has served as a High Court [judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judge "Judge") in [Saint Lucia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucia "Saint Lucia") and a Court of Appeal judge in Barbados, and was the first woman admitted to the [bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_(law) "Bar (law)") in Barbados. She served as chair of the [CARICOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARICOM "CARICOM") commission to evaluate regional integration, was the first magistrate appointed an [ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambassador "Ambassador") from Barbados, and was the first woman to serve on the country's [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_Supreme_Court "Barbados Supreme Court"). She was the first appointee from Barbados to the Commonwealth Secretariat Arbitral Tribunal. In 2017, she was appointed the 8th governor-general of Barbados, with a term beginning on 8 January 2018. Simultaneously with her appointment, Mason was awarded the Dame Grand Cross in the [Order of Saint Michael and Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Saint_Michael_and_Saint_George "Order of Saint Michael and Saint George"). On assumption of the office of Governor-General, she became the Chancellor of the [Order of National Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_National_Heroes "Order of National Heroes"), [Order of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Barbados "Order of Barbados") and the [Order of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Freedom_of_Barbados "Order of Freedom of Barbados").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Sandra Prunella Mason was born on 17 January 1949[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) in [Saint Philip, Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Philip,_Barbados "Saint Philip, Barbados").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-(CSAT)-4) After studying at St. Catherine's Primary School until age nine, she attended secondary school at [Queen's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_College_(Barbados) "Queen's College (Barbados)"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-BarbadosGov-5) then began teaching at the Princess Margaret Secondary School in 1968.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-6) The following year, she worked at [Barclays Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Bank "Barclays Bank") as a clerk. Mason enrolled in the [University of the West Indies at Cave Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_West_Indies_at_Cave_Hill "University of the West Indies at Cave Hill"), where she earned a [Bachelor of Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Laws "Bachelor of Laws").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) Mason was one of the first graduates of the Faculty of Law from UWI, Cave Hill, completing her education in 1973.

In 1975, she obtained a [Legal Education Certificate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_Education_Certificate "Legal Education Certificate") from [Hugh Wooding Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Wooding_Law_School "Hugh Wooding Law School") in [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago "Trinidad and Tobago"), becoming the first woman attorney-at-law from Barbados to graduate from the school.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-BarbadosGov-5) She was [admitted to the bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admitted_to_the_bar "Admitted to the bar") on 10 November the same year,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrathwaite1999287-7) becoming the first woman member of the Barbados Bar Association.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) She is a [Soroptimist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soroptimist_International "Soroptimist International") and Patron of SI Barbados.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-8)

## Early career and legal practice

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career and legal practice")]

Beginning in 1975, she worked in Trust Administration for Barclay's and transferred to several different posts within the Barclay's company until 1977.

In 1978, Mason began working as the Magistrate of the Juvenile and Family Court and simultaneously tutoring in family law at UWI. She stopped tutoring in 1983 and continued working as a magistrate. In 1988, Mason completed the [Royal Institute of Public Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_Public_Administration "Royal Institute of Public Administration") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")'s course on Judicial Administration.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) She served on the UN [Committee on the Rights of the Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_on_the_Rights_of_the_Child "Committee on the Rights of the Child") from its 1991 inception until 1999, holding the vice chair from 1993 to 1995 and chair from 1997 to 1999.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEricksonCohenHart2001231-9)

Between 1991 and 1992, Mason served as chair[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) and was one of the two women appointed to the 13-member [CARICOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARICOM "CARICOM") commission charged with evaluating regional integration.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-(CSAT)-4) She left the family court in 1992[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) to serve as an ambassador to Venezuela, and was the first woman magistrate from Barbados to serve in that position. Between 1993 and 1994 she also served as ambassador to [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"), [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") and [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-BarbadosGov-5) Upon her return to Barbados[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrathwaite1999287-7) in 1994, Mason was appointed Chief Magistrate for Barbados, and in 1997 became the Registrar of the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Barbados "Supreme Court of Barbados").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-appellate_judge-10)

In 2000, Mason completed studies on Alternative Dispute Resolution at the [University of Windsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Windsor_Faculty_of_Law "University of Windsor Faculty of Law") in [Windsor, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor,_Ontario "Windsor, Ontario"), Canada, and then completed a Fellowship with the [Commonwealth Judicial Education Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Judicial_Education_Institute?action=edit&redlink=1 "Commonwealth Judicial Education Institute (page does not exist)") in [Halifax, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax,_Nova_Scotia "Halifax, Nova Scotia"), in 2001, as well as a course in Advanced Dispute Resolution at UWI.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) She continued to serve as Registrar of the Supreme Court until 2005, when she was appointed as Queen's Counsel to the Inner Bar of Barbados.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) In 2008, Mason was sworn in as an Appeals Judge[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-appellate_judge-10) becoming the first woman to serve on the Barbados Court of Appeals.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Caribbean_Elections_bio-3) For three days in 2012, she became the acting Governor-General of Barbados[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-Acting_GG-11) and the following year was the first Barbadian appointed to membership in the [Commonwealth Secretariat Arbitral Tribunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Secretariat_Arbitral_Tribunal "Commonwealth Secretariat Arbitral Tribunal") (CSAT). The Tribunal operates among members of the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") to resolve issues concerning contract disputes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-(CSAT)-4) With that appointment, _Loop News_ named her one of the 10 most powerful women in Barbados.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-10_most_powerful-12)

## Governor-General of Barbados

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Governor-General of Barbados")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/2020_Independence_Day_Parade_and_National_Awards_Ceremony_%2850665847882%29.jpg/250px-2020_Independence_Day_Parade_and_National_Awards_Ceremony_%2850665847882%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2020_Independence_Day_Parade_and_National_Awards_Ceremony_(50665847882).jpg)

Mason presenting National Awards during the 2020 Independence Day parade

In 2017, Mason was appointed as the eighth Governor-General of Barbados, with a term beginning on 8 January 2018. Simultaneously with her appointment, Mason was also appointed a Dame Grand Cross in the [Order of Saint Michael and Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Saint_Michael_and_Saint_George "Order of Saint Michael and Saint George").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-13)

In 2020, Mason, in her official capacity announcing government policy in the [Throne Speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throne_Speech "Throne Speech"), written by the government of Prime Minister [Mia Mottley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_Mottley "Mia Mottley"), stated that [Barbados would become a republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_Barbados "Republicanism in Barbados"), abolishing the [Barbadian monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Barbados "Monarchy of Barbados").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-14) She was then expected to be nominated as a candidate to be the first president of Barbados, then to be elected by the two houses of parliament, and to assume office on 30 November 2021.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-17)

## President of Barbados

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sandra_Mason&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: President of Barbados")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Barbados_Independence_Republic_Night_%2851717663162%29.jpg/250px-Barbados_Independence_Republic_Night_%2851717663162%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barbados_Independence_Republic_Night_(51717663162).jpg)

Mason taking oath as the first president of Barbados, 2021

On 12 October 2021, Mason was nominated by Prime Minister [Mia Mottley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_Mottley "Mia Mottley") and Opposition Leader [Joseph Atherley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Atherley "Joseph Atherley") to become the first [president of Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Barbados "President of Barbados").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-18) On 20 October she was [elected by both houses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Barbadian_presidential_election "2021 Barbadian presidential election") without opposition.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-19) Mason took office on 30 November 2021,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-:0-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-21) the 55th anniversary of [Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados_Independence_Act_1966 "Barbados Independence Act 1966"). While she is nominally chief executive and is the sole head of state in Barbados, in practice her role is mostly ceremonial, much like her previous role as Governor-General.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-22) She made her first official visit to [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") in June 2022.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-23)

As president, Mason represented Barbados at the [state funeral of Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_funeral_of_Queen_Elizabeth_II "State funeral of Queen Elizabeth II") in 2022, and at the [coronation of King Charles III and Queen Camilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation_of_King_Charles_III_and_Queen_Camilla "Coronation of King Charles III and Queen Camilla") in 2023.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Mason#cite_note-25)
